title: Baseline retest for cores/bench
Shared radix-4 combinational divider for RV32M
motivation:
The only recorded experiment is the baseline: fitness 12.12 at median
Fmax 5.442 MHz, with a 199.837 ns, 156-cell worst path traversing
forwarding and the EX-stage ALU. The ALU expresses signed and unsigned
division and remainder as separate / and % operators. These operations
are the strongest explanation for the exceptionally deep arithmetic path.
Optimizing their combinational implementation can raise Fmax without
adding execution cycles or changing CoreMark's memory-stall behavior.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace only the real DIV/DIVU/REM/REMU datapath with one shared, fully
combinational unsigned radix-4 restoring divider. Preserve the ALU ports,
zero-cycle ALU latency, five-stage pipeline, forwarding, bus handshakes,
and nret=1 retirement contract. This is a local arithmetic-network
optimization, with no iterative unit, extra registers, or pipeline stalls.

For DIV and REM, convert each operand to its unsigned two's-complement
magnitude; DIVU and REMU use the original unsigned operands. Precompute
zero-extended divisor multiples D, 2D, and 3D in 34 bits so overflow is
impossible. Unroll sixteen stages, consuming dividend bit pairs from
most significant to least significant. Each stage forms the 34-bit trial
remainder T = (R << 2) | next_pair and computes T-D, T-2D, and T-3D
in parallel as 35-bit zero-extended subtractions. Their high borrow bits
select the largest nonnegative subtraction and hence quotient digit
0, 1, 2, or 3. Reuse each subtraction's result for the selected remainder
rather than placing a second subtractor after the digit selection.
For nonzero D, the selected remainder is less than D and fits in 32 bits.
Assemble the quotient from the sixteen digits and obtain the remainder
directly from the final stage, without a quotient-times-divisor multiply.

Negate the quotient iff signed division has differing operand signs;
negate the remainder iff signed remainder has a negative dividend.
Explicitly retain divide-by-zero quotient 0xffffffff and remainder a,
and signed INT_MIN/-1 quotient INT_MIN and remainder zero. Leave every
RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS expression and all non-division ALU operations intact.
The intended gain comes from reducing serial quotient-decision stages
from 32 to 16 and sharing the magnitude engine across all four operations.
Parallel subtractor area and digit-selection routing are the principal
risks; vendor timing must confirm that their cost is outweighed by the
shorter serial path. With unchanged cycle count, a Fmax gain above 4.6%
translates directly into a qualifying fitness improvement.

title: Move division out of the single-cycle execute path
motivation:
The baseline reaches only 5.442 MHz and reports a 199.837 ns, 156-cell
path through forwarding and the execute ALU. The ALU implements signed
and unsigned division and remainder with combinational / and % operators;
their unrolled arithmetic is a strong candidate for this extreme depth.
These circuits constrain every instruction's clock period, even when no
division is executing. The experiment history contains only the baseline,
with no previous structural attempt or LESSONS.md to rule out this change.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace the combinational DIV/DIVU/REM/REMU hardware with one blocking,
registered, radix-2 restoring divider shared by quotient and remainder.
Perform one unsigned divide iteration per clock for 32 iterations, with
registered operand normalization and result sign correction. Keep all
other integer operations, including multiplication, on their existing
execution path. This is one structural change: isolate variable-latency
division from the fast single-cycle ALU, rather than redesign the pipeline.

On a valid divide instruction, accept exactly one request when the older
MEM instruction is not blocking EX. Capture the fully forwarded rs1/rs2,
operation and instruction metadata before older forwarding sources drain.
Hold the fetch PC and ID/EX instruction until the result can advance;
allow older MEM/WB instructions to drain exactly once. While division is
running, inject invalid EX/MEM bubbles with register-write and memory
controls cleared, rather than repeatedly emitting or freezing the older
instruction. Latch completion until EX/MEM can accept it, advance the
divide exactly once, and then release the upstream hold. Existing dmem
backpressure retains priority, and divider request/result handshakes must
be qualified by instruction validity and reset. The completed instruction
uses the captured source values for RVFI and the normal forwarding and
retirement path, preserving nret=1 and contiguous channel-0 orders.

Normalize signed operands into unsigned magnitudes; use a 33-bit partial
remainder and one compare/subtract/shift step per cycle. Correct quotient
sign from the operand-sign XOR and remainder sign from the dividend.
Explicitly implement divide-by-zero and INT_MIN/-1 results for all four
operations. Under RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS, retain the existing exact algebraic
substitutions through the ordinary single-cycle ALU path so bounded
pipeline proofs remain tractable. Real simulation and synthesis must use
the iterative divider and must contain no combinational / or % hardware
feeding the fast ALU result. Retain full arithmetic coverage by migrating
divider vectors to a handshake-aware divider test, without dropping the
existing correctness assertions or weakening any evaluator checks.

The prediction is that the substantial reduction in ALU depth and divider
area outweighs the additional division cycles in the marked CoreMark
region. Measure the product of median Gowin Fmax and bracketed iterations
per cycle, not Fmax alone. A greater than 4.6 percent fitness increase is
required; the 50 percent estimate is the schema's capped forecast, not a
measured result. Keep all bus ports, decoder legality and trap handling,
multiplication semantics, memory ordering and evaluation files intact.

title: Small tagged next-PC predictor with two-bit branch hysteresis
motivation:
The baseline predicts every control transfer as fall-through and flushes
the younger fetched instruction for every taken branch, JAL, and JALR.
IF/ID is combinational, so this is a one-cycle recovery bubble, not the
two-cycle penalty of a pipeline with a separate IF/ID register. Repeated
CoreMark loops and calls should make many of these bubbles avoidable.
No predictor attempts are recorded in the bench experiment history.
The measured critical path runs through the combinational M-extension
arithmetic; a small PC-indexed table should improve iterations/cycle
without adding logic to that arithmetic path.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add one compact next-PC predictor: a 64-entry direct-mapped tagged BTB
indexed by fetch PC[7:2], with full remaining PC tags, aligned 32-bit
targets, a conditional/unconditional bit, and a two-bit saturating
direction counter per entry. A matching unconditional entry predicts
its last resolved target; a conditional entry predicts its target only
when the counter MSB is set. Misses predict PC+4. Initialize a newly
allocated conditional entry weakly toward its resolved outcome. Train
both branch outcomes, learn JAL/JALR targets, and refresh indirect
targets on resolution. Do not add a return stack or global history.

Lookup uses only the registered fetch PC, not an instruction-memory
decode or a forwarding-dependent operand. Store full targets rather
than adding branch immediates on the fetch critical path. Reset entry
valid bits, and keep invalid payloads unobservable; avoid resetting the
tag/target arrays so the vendor can infer distributed storage. Keep the
predictor small enough that its lookup and PC mux remain well below the
existing divider path. Do not change arithmetic or pipeline depth.

Carry the exact selected predicted_next_pc with every accepted fetch
through IF/ID and ID/EX. EX computes the architectural next PC using
the existing forwarded operands and alignment/trap rules. Redirect and
squash the younger instruction only when that actual next PC differs
from the carried prediction. Compare successors for every valid EX
instruction, including ordinary and illegal instructions, so stale
entries cannot silently skip instructions. A correctly predicted taken
branch or jump must neither flush ID nor discard a ready target fetch.
RVFI pc_wdata always reports the architectural successor, never the
prediction; JAL/JALR link data remains the original instruction PC+4.

Advance the predicted fetch PC only when the current instruction is
accepted: imem ready, no load-use hold, no dmem hold, and no recovery.
Define resolve_fire as a valid EX instruction advancing to EX/MEM.
Qualify both predictor training and recovery with resolve_fire, so a
dmem-stalled branch neither retrains repeatedly nor redirects while
frozen. Once EX can advance, recovery has priority over imem stalls and
load-use holds, preserving the existing redirect-override requirement.
Metadata holds with its instruction and clears on bubbles/squashes.
Train only legal, aligned control transfers; invalidate a matching
stale entry when its PC resolves as a non-control or faulting instruction.

The prediction is that removing most recurring taken-control bubbles
reduces the marked CoreMark cycle count sufficiently to clear the 4.6%
acceptance margin at similar median Gowin Fmax. Preserve nret=1, the
top-level bus contract, decoder legality, all RVFI rules, and all eval
checks. Validate with directed pipeline tests, normal formal and cosim,
canonical CoreMark CRC/UART checks under both bus stalls, and vendor
timing; no performance improvement is claimed before those measurements.

title: Remove redirect feedback from decode operand and hazard paths
motivation:
The current champion scores 95.23 at median Gowin Fmax 42.774 MHz.
Its reported worst path is 29.042 ns and 51 cells, from register-file
storage to an ID/EX rs2_val register, crossing u_id, u_ex, u_if,
u_hazard, and u_id again. The RTL masks the fetched instruction to
a NOP on EX redirect or imem unavailability, putting late redirect
logic ahead of register-file addressing, decode, and load-use compares.
ID also clears its entire wide register on flush. This creates a
control-to-data feedback cone that can limit every instruction's clock.
The prior micro_opt attempt optimized the old combinational divider
and reached only 13.23; the champion already removed that bottleneck.
There is no LESSONS.md and no recorded attempt on this new critical path.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Make one local optimization: represent fetch/decode bubbles with an
invalid bit and cleared control bits, rather than transforming the
instruction and resetting its operand payload. Keep the pipeline
depth, instruction acceptance schedule, branch penalty, iterative
divider, arithmetic, bus protocol, and nret=1 retirement boundary.

In IF, pass raw imem_data to the instruction payload independently of
redirect and imemReady. Use the existing flush/redirect conditions
only to deassert payload validity. Keep redirect priority over PC
stalls. In ID, decode and address the register file from these raw
instruction bits, and split ID/EX updates into data and control.
Preserve deterministic reset, but remove flush and fetch validity
from the enables and D-input muxes of pc, operands, immediate,
instruction, and register-address payload flops. These fields may
capture normally when ID is not held, or retain their previous values
on a bubble; their values are irrelevant when valid is zero.

On a permitted flush, clear ID/EX valid and the entire ctrl_t even
if the ordinary stall input is asserted for a load-use bubble. On
ordinary advancement, latch decoded controls only for a valid fetch;
otherwise clear ctrl_t and valid. On a genuine dmem/divider hold,
preserve the complete live ID/EX instruction, including its controls
and operands. Never clear controls merely because fetch validity is
low during such a hold. Preserve the current hazard priority that
suppresses flush_id while dmem or execute hold prevents advancement.
Clearing controls is mandatory: invalidity alone does not suppress
the current forwarding, memory, and load-hazard consumers.

Feed load-use comparisons directly from raw fetched rs1/rs2 fields,
independent of redirect, flush_if, or redirect-derived fetch validity.
If qualification is needed, use imemReady and the registered EX load
control, never the redirect-dependent IF valid signal. The bubble's
cleared mem_read prevents stale ID/EX destinations from causing a
hazard on the next cycle. Leave redirects with priority over PC hold
and preserve real load-use, dmem, and divider stalls. Do not reintroduce
the removed path through source-address zeroing, a masked instruction
alias, a wide output mask, or data-register enables driven by flush.

The expected effect is a shorter EX-redirect feedback path and lower
flush fanout, improving Gowin Fmax with essentially unchanged marked
CoreMark cycles. A 15 percent fitness gain is a forecast, not a
measurement. Other EX or register-file paths may become limiting.
Validate the existing formal, unit-test, cosim, canonical CoreMark
CRC/UART and marker checks without weakening them, then compare median
Gowin Fmax times iterations/cycle against the 95.23 champion. Accept
only a measured improvement exceeding the 4.6 percent margin.

title: Resolve control-flow redirects from the EX/MEM register
motivation:
The structural divider hypothesis is the current champion: fitness 95.23,
median Gowin Fmax 42.774 MHz, and 4,491,817 marked CoreMark cycles. It
removed the combinational division bottleneck; its new worst path is
29.042 ns through u_id, u_ex, u_if, u_hazard, and back into u_id. The
current EX branch comparison drives fetch instruction replacement and
ID/EX flush control in the same cycle. Registering this recovery decision
should interrupt that long control path. LESSONS.md is absent, and the
history contains no attempt to retime redirects. The earlier predictor
experiment retained the baseline divider bottleneck and does not measure
this structural change on the champion.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Move architectural redirect application from combinational EX resolution
to the existing EX/MEM register. Keep branch comparisons, JAL/JALR target
calculation, and alignment checks in EX, but capture their resolved
control-flow outcome with the instruction. Drive fetch recovery only
from that registered, valid, legal outcome. This is one structural
change to the recovery boundary; retain the champion's iterative divider
and ordinary ALU, register file, memory stages, and nret=1 contract.

Use the registered EX/MEM branch_taken, ctrl.is_jump, ctrl.is_illegal,
and pc_next fields, or equivalent explicit registered recovery fields.

its recorded architectural successor. Not-taken branches, bubbles, and
faulting control transfers generate none. Leave RVFI pc_wdata, JAL/JALR
link values, trap semantics, and operand snapshots architectural; delaying

and from combinational instruction substitution. Avoid adding a direct

During registered recovery, redirect the PC and squash both younger
instructions: the fetched/decode instruction and the instruction already
in EX. EX/MEM must receive an invalid, side-effect-free bubble instead
of the younger EX result. Let the older redirecting instruction advance
through MEM/WB and retire exactly once. Give recovery priority over

launches and execute_hold with the EX squash so a wrong-path DIV/REM

older MEM load/store remains in EX until it can enter EX/MEM; it cannot

This adds one recovery bubble per taken branch or jump while leaving

improvement alone. The principal risks are the added branch bubbles and

Preserve every existing correctness gate and all evaluation-side files.

title: Timing-aware tagged branch prediction on the iterative-divider core
motivation:
The current core fetches PC+4 and discards the younger instruction on
every taken branch, JAL, and JALR. IF/ID is combinational, so each such
recovery costs one bubble. The prior predictor experiment reduced the
marked CoreMark cycle count from 4491485 to 4197517, a 6.5% reduction,
but its 5.557 MHz timing and 12641 LUTs still reflected the old
combinational-divider implementation. The current iterative-divider
champion runs at 42.774 MHz and 95.23 iterations/second; its critical
path now crosses EX redirect, IF, and hazard control. Recovering the
demonstrated predictor cycle benefit therefore requires protecting
this new timing path, rather than restoring the previous RTL base.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add a single 64-entry direct-mapped tagged branch-target predictor to
the CURRENT iterative-divider core. Index by fetch PC[7:2], compare all
remaining PC bits, and store an aligned full-width target, valid bit,
conditional/unconditional bit, and two-bit saturating direction counter.
A conditional hit predicts taken when its counter MSB is set; an
unconditional hit predicts its last resolved target. A miss predicts
PC+4. Allocate a conditional entry weakly toward the resolved outcome,
train both outcomes, and refresh JAL/JALR targets when they resolve.
Use only the registered PC for table lookup, with no instruction-memory
decode or operand forwarding in the prediction-to-PC path. Reset valid
bits; allow invalid tag/target payloads to remain unreset and unobserved.
Do not add global history, a return stack, caches, or arithmetic changes.

Make prediction validation timing-aware. Carry predicted_taken and the
exact selected target with the fetched instruction into ID. In ID,
precompute and register PC+4 and the direct branch/JAL target PC+imm,
and compare that direct target against the carried predicted target.
Carry the resulting direct_target_match bit, predicted_taken, and the
selected target into ID/EX. EX must use the registered direct target and
fall-through address for recovery and architectural pc_next, avoiding
an EX target adder followed by a full next-PC equality comparison on
every branch. For direct branches, recovery is a taken-direction
mismatch or a taken prediction with a false direct_target_match. JAL
uses the same registered target-match check. Only JALR needs the EX
forwarded-rs1-plus-immediate target comparison, after clearing bit zero.
Define actual_taken as a legal, aligned taken branch or legal, aligned
jump. If a stale entry predicts taken for an ordinary, illegal, or
faulting instruction, actual_taken is false and recovery selects the
registered PC+4. A prediction may never silently skip a non-control
instruction. Trap, link-write, and architectural successor semantics
must remain identical to the existing implementation.

Qualify recovery and training with resolve_fire: a valid instruction
transferring out of EX into EX/MEM, with neither a dmem freeze nor an
unfinished divider operation. A frozen branch must not repeatedly
train or move the fetch PC. A correctly predicted transfer must allow
the ready target instruction to enter ID/EX without a flush. An accepted
recovery squashes that younger instruction and overrides imem stalls
and load-use holds. Otherwise the PC follows the predicted successor
only when imem is ready and the fetched instruction is actually accepted
by ID/EX. Metadata holds and clears with its instruction. Preserve the
divider's request/result handshake, upstream hold, saved operands and
metadata, completion transfer, and downstream bubble/drain behavior.

Avoid extending the existing redirect-to-flush feedback path: compute
load-use comparisons from raw fetched instruction bits, independently
of the redirect-controlled NOP mux, and give an accepted recovery
explicit priority in hazard control. Load-use detection is relevant
only for an available fetch that could otherwise be accepted. Preserve
imem bubbles, load-use bubbles, dmem freezes, and MEM/WB data retention
with valid clearing. Train only legal aligned control transfers on
resolve_fire, and invalidate a matching stale entry when a non-control
or faulting instruction resolves. Table replacement initializes its
own counter rather than inheriting the aliased entry's state.

Keep nret=1, external ports, decoder legality checks, memory bounds,
RVFI retirement ordering, and all evaluation contracts unchanged.
Architectural RVFI pc_wdata must report the resolved successor;
JAL/JALR link data remains PC+4. Update packed-bundle unit-test helpers
when adding fields. Validate predictor collisions and training, then
directed pipeline cases with correct and incorrect predictions under
both bus stalls and divider holds, normal formal and cosim, and canonical
CoreMark UART/CRC validation. Evaluate median Gowin Fmax times marked
iterations/cycle. At the earlier predictor's approximately 7% cycle-rate
gain, clearing the 4.6% acceptance margin requires roughly 41.8 MHz or
better; extra predictor IPC is not sufficient if recovery logic reduces
Fmax materially. This is an unmeasured proposal, not a claimed result.

title: Share one signedness-selectable DSP multiplier across RV32M products
motivation:
The champion scores 111.35 at median Gowin Fmax 50.016 MHz and
4491817 marker-bounded CoreMark cycles. Its remaining worst path
crosses mul_uu and the surrounding execute muxes. The ALU currently
expresses three full-width products for signed-signed, unsigned-unsigned
and signed-unsigned multiplication, consuming six DSP blocks. The last
successful micro-optimization shortened control feedback without adding
execution cycles. Sharing multiplication is a similarly local way to
reduce DSP routing and result-selection overhead without reducing IPC.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace the three real multiplication expressions with exactly one
signed 33-by-33-bit multiplication whose extra operand bits encode
signedness. This is solely a combinational multiplier resource-sharing
optimization; retain the champion's pipeline and execution schedule.

Compute a_signed = (op == ALU_MULH || op == ALU_MULHSU) and
b_signed = (op == ALU_MULH). Form signed 33-bit operands
A = $signed({a_signed && a[31], a}) and
B = $signed({b_signed && b[31], b}), and compute one signed 66-bit
product P = A * B. MUL uses P[31:0]; MULH, MULHU and MULHSU share
P[63:32] through a single grouped case arm. Zero extension for MUL
is valid because low product bits are independent of signedness.
Keep the sign-control gates confined to the two extension bits;
the original 32 data bits must feed the multiplier directly, without
operand-wide mode muxes. Declare intermediate signedness and widths
explicitly so SystemVerilog expression sizing cannot truncate the
product or interpret an unsigned operand as negative. Bits P[65:64]
are intentionally unused. Avoid serial signed-correction subtractors
or fabric-added limb products, which lengthen the measured path.

Gowin should map the common product into one wide DSP multiplier
instead of three distinct engines, removing redundant arithmetic
blocks and simplifying the output selection and physical routing.
Preserve every exact RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS expression independently:
its three add/XOR and one subtract/XOR multiply substitutes must not
be collapsed into the real shared product. Keep real DIV/REM in the
existing blocking divider. Retain all other ALU operations, decoder
legality, forwarding, stall and redirect priorities, memory behavior,
nret=1 ports, RVFI source values and exactly-once ordered retirement.

A temporary prototype of this exact expression and grouped high-half
result arm passed 20400 real multiplication checks covering directed
edges and 5000 seeded random operand pairs across all four operations.
All 19 existing pipeline tests also passed on the prototype.
Gowin placement options 0/1/2 reached 52.491/54.960/54.960 MHz,
giving median 54.960 MHz, 9.88 percent above the champion's 50.016 MHz.
Option 0 also improved from its reproduced 47.922 MHz, a 9.53 percent
matched-option increase. Area was 2499 versus 2502 LUTs, unchanged
678 registers and two versus six DSP blocks. These vendor timing and
arithmetic measurements are not a completed fitness evaluation;
full correctness gates and marked CoreMark simulation remain required.
At unchanged 4491817 marked cycles, exceeding the 4.6 percent champion
margin requires median Fmax above 52.317 MHz. Placement-dependent
routing and the operation-dependent sign-bit path are the main risks.
Validate exact arithmetic, existing ALTOPS, pipeline and cosim checks,
formal gates and canonical CoreMark UART/CRC/marker checks, then compare
median Gowin Fmax times measured marker-bounded iterations/cycle.

title: Isolate wide multiplication in a registered partial-product unit
motivation:
The champion scores 111.35 at median Gowin Fmax 50.016 MHz and
4,491,817 marked CoreMark cycles. Moving division into a sequential
unit previously raised fitness from 12.12 to 95.23. The subsequent
redirect/decode cleanup reached the present champion, whose reported
worst path is 26.162 ns through the register file, ID, EX and ALU to
data memory. A fresh make timing TARGET=bench reproduces placement
option 0 at 47.922 MHz and shows the worst two paths passing through
u_alu/mul_uu_63_s0/DOUT, confirming the multiplier is on these paths.
The ALU evaluates three unregistered 32-bit multiplication expressions
for MUL/MULH/MULHU/MULHSU. No multiplication
isolation attempt appears in the structural history. The other
structural attempt delayed every taken branch and jump and scored
only 107.09: extra recovery cycles outweighed its modest Fmax gain.
LESSONS.md is absent. This proposal instead charges additional
latency only to multiplication and leaves ordinary branch recovery.
Profiling the canonical 2K -O3 ELF through the unchanged Python ISS
counts 93,960 multiplies among 2,922,015 instructions between markers,
all MUL rather than high-half variants. A diagnostic copy with real
multiply outputs replaced by constants reaches 60.247 MHz on option 0
and shortens the worst path to 21.893 ns. This diagnostic deliberately
lacks multiplication semantics; it measures timing potential only,
not an implemented candidate's Fmax or fitness.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Move all real MUL/MULH/MULHU/MULHSU computation out of the ordinary
combinational EX ALU into one blocking registered multiplier. Share
one unsigned 32-by-32 product across all four operations, implemented
with four explicitly bounded unsigned 16-by-16 partial products.
Register operands before the partial products, and register the
accumulation and sign-correction boundaries so neither forwarding
plus multiplication nor multiplication plus a wide accumulation can
remain in a single clock path. This is one structural change to the
execution unit, not a general pipeline or control-flow redesign.

Use a concrete schedule: edge 1 accepts and captures fully forwarded
operands and operation; edge 2 registers the four 16-by-16 products;
edge 3 registers the 33-bit sum of the two cross products. MUL can
complete on edge 3, using its low word directly: its low 16 bits are
p00[15:0], and its upper 16 bits are the modulo-2^16 sum of
p00[31:16], p01[15:0] and p10[15:0]. Use a three-input carry-save
compression followed by one 16-bit carry-propagate addition to avoid
two serial additions on this frequent path. This result uses the
same registered partial products, not a second multiplier.

For high-half operations, edge 4 assembles and registers the unsigned
high word from p11 and the full cross sum; MULHU completes there.
Signed-high operations complete on edge 5 with sign correction.
In parallel with these stages,
compute and register the modulo-2^32 correction term: b when a is
negative for MULH or MULHSU, plus a when b is negative for MULH.
MUL and MULHU use no correction. The signed high result is the
unsigned high word minus this correction.
Implement assembly by first forming the 17-bit sum of the low
product's upper half and the cross sum's lower half, then using its
carry in the high-word addition. Retain full cross-term carry width.
Keep the ordinary MUL result independent of these later stages. If
Gowin timing requires another register, account for that extra
multiply cycle in the fitness comparison. Do not implement
any combinational 32-by-32 multiplier on the ordinary ALU output.

Reuse the successful divider's blocking execution protocol. Accept
a multiply request exactly once when the valid legal EX instruction
can advance past older data-memory backpressure; snapshot its entire
instruction and RVFI operand metadata at acceptance. Hold PC and
ID/EX beginning with the request cycle, while older instructions drain
and EX/MEM receives bubbles with every side-effect control cleared.
Retain a completed result until EX/MEM can accept it; transfer the
saved instruction and result once on the same edge that releases
the upstream hold. MUL with rd=x0 still retires normally. Preserve
MEM/WB data retention for forwarding during data-memory stalls,
reset cancellation, and the existing divider without relaunching a
held multiply or allowing a younger instruction to execute early.

Under RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS, retain all exact existing M-operation
substitutions in the ordinary single-cycle ALU and disable the real
multiplier hold, as the current divider integration already does.
Real simulation and FPGA synthesis must exercise the new multiplier.
Move existing real multiply vectors into a sequential-unit suite
without reducing arithmetic coverage. Keep decoder legality, memory
alignment traps, nret=1 ports, channel-0 retirement ordering and all
evaluator files intact. Ordinary RV32I operations, EX redirects,
load-use bubbles and instruction-memory readiness retain their
present behavior.

The expected tradeoff is substantially higher Fmax against several
extra cycles per multiply in CoreMark's matrix work. Edge-3 MUL
completion is consumed into EX/MEM on edge 4, versus edge 1 for the
champion: nominally 281,880 added clocks, or 6.28 percent of the
champion's marked cycles. At this cost, the acceptance threshold
requires about 55.6 MHz rather than the current 50.016 MHz. Changing
the pseudo-random bus-stall alignment can alter the actual cycle
count; the estimate is not a simulation result. The 12 percent
fitness forecast is unmeasured. Validate real arithmetic, pipeline
dependencies and bus stalls, formal and retirement cosim, then require
the canonical CoreMark CRCs, UART success literal and timing markers.
Success requires (new median Gowin Fmax / 50.016 MHz) times

title: Instruction-qualified direction prediction without a target table
motivation:
The champion already removes redirect from raw fetch/decode payloads
and reaches 111.35 iterations/second at 50.016 MHz. The previous
64-entry tagged predictor reduced marked CoreMark cycles from
4491817 to 4197447, but its 45.983 MHz clock erased the gain. Its
critical path crossed EX recovery, IF, immediate decoding, and the
ID direct_target_match register. Recovering predictable direct-control
bubbles is worthwhile only if prediction avoids that feedback cone.
A reference-ISS profile of the canonical -O3, 2K, 10-iteration ELF
between its MMIO markers found 294425 taken conditional branches,
49367 JALs, and only 13735 JALRs. A 32-entry direction-table replay
produced 55558 conditional misses, removing 288234 net control bubbles
in this software model while leaving JALR unpredicted. The UART had
the canonical five CRCs and the validation literal. These are trace
statistics, not a measured RTL cycle count or Gowin fitness result.
There is no LESSONS.md in this fixture. Both prior predictor outcomes
were reviewed in experiments/log.jsonl before selecting this approach.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add one instruction-qualified, direction-only predictor to the CURRENT
champion. Use a 32-entry PC-indexed bimodal table of two-bit saturating
counters, indexed by fetch PC[6:2], initialized weakly not taken.
Consult it only for a positively validated conditional BRANCH encoding.
Predict every legal aligned JAL taken using its actual instruction
immediate. Leave JALR prediction as fall-through. There is no target
table, PC tag, return stack, global history, or indirect-target cache.

Compute the exact B/J target and PC+4 from the unmodified fetched PC
and raw io_imemData before the ID/EX boundary. The same direct-target
wire drives the predicted PC selection and the ID/EX direct_target
register; it is not a remembered target requiring comparison. Require
direct-target word alignment before predicting taken. Reserved branch
encodings and ordinary/illegal instructions always predict fall-through.
The direction table aliases may affect performance but cannot change
targets or architectural behavior. Latch the selected predicted_taken
bit, direct_target and fallthrough_pc with the original instruction.

In EX use the registered direct target and fall-through address for
branch/JAL resolution, link results, traps, recovery, and RVFI pc_next.
A legal aligned conditional branch needs recovery only when its actual
taken direction differs from its carried predicted_taken bit; no
32-bit predicted-target equality or direct_target_match register is
needed. A correctly predicted JAL requires no recovery. JALR still
resolves through the existing forwarded operand and immediate path and
recovers to its actual aligned target. Preserve existing misalignment
traps, including no link write and architectural fall-through on fault.
For correctness, any unexpected predicted_taken on a non-control or
faulting instruction must recover to its registered fall-through PC.

Preserve the champion's separation of payload from squash control.
out.instr remains raw imem_data on every cycle. Prediction decode,
immediate extraction, target addition, register-file addresses,
load-use source comparisons, and all prediction/address payload D
inputs must be independent of recovery, flush, and fetch validity.
The new ID/EX payload registers use the same reset and ordinary hold
conditions as pc/imm, with no flush reset or recovery-dependent enable.
Only valid and ctrl_t clear on an allowed squash or unavailable fetch;
invalid prediction metadata is ignored. Do not mask instruction bits,
zero source addresses, or clear the wide payload on a recovery.

Advance the PC to the selected prediction only when imem is ready and
the fetched instruction is accepted by ID/EX. During a load-use bubble,
imem stall, dmem freeze, or divider hold retain the appropriate PC and
live metadata. Qualify training and recovery with a valid instruction
actually advancing out of EX, not a held branch. Accepted recovery
overrides imem and load-use holds, but waits until older dmem freezes
permit EX advancement. Correct predictions neither flush ID nor
discard a ready target fetch. Update exactly one conditional counter
per accepted legal aligned branch, saturating up/down on its actual
outcome; do not update for jumps, bubbles, traps, or repeated hold
cycles. Preserve the iterative divider and MEM/WB forwarding retention.

The forecast is a 7 percent fitness gain from direct-control bubble
removal with approximately unchanged Fmax. Omitting JALR prediction
trades some cycle benefit for a much smaller prediction/recovery cone.
The software replay suggests approximately 4203583 cycles if each net
bubble removed translated to one measured cycle, a 6.86 percent rate
gain at the champion clock. That is only an estimate: bus-stall
overlap, speculative fetches and delayed counter training can change
it. At that cycle estimate the 4.6 percent acceptance margin requires
approximately 49.0 MHz; protecting Fmax is the main uncertainty.
Measure marked CoreMark
cycles and median Gowin Fmax rather than treating cycle savings alone
as success. Keep nret=1, all ports, decoder legality, architectural
retirement data, and every existing formal/cosim/CRC/UART/marker gate.

title: Shorten EX operand delivery with registered dependency matches
motivation:
The champion scores 122.36 at median Gowin Fmax 54.96 MHz and
4491817 marker-bounded CoreMark cycles. Its 24.345 ns worst path
starts at MEM/WB rd and crosses forwarding, operand muxes and the
shared multiplier. Detailed vendor reports also expose competing
register-file BRAM-output paths through the same EX arithmetic:
Gowin absorbs ID/EX operand registers into memory output registers,
leaving a 2.260 ns BRAM clock-to-output delay on the EX operand path.
The prior registered multiplier added 282019 marked cycles and scored
117.73 despite higher Fmax. Prior micro_opt experiments addressed the
old divider, redirect feedback and multiplier sharing; none retimed
dependency comparisons. LESSONS.md is absent. Operand delivery can
be shortened locally without adding any instruction execution cycles.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Make one micro optimization to EX operand delivery: compute register
dependency matches before the ID/EX edge and keep the register-file
operand boundary in ordinary flip-flops. Retain the pipeline topology,
instruction acceptance schedule and all arithmetic latencies. This
is a timing-oriented implementation of the existing operand network,
with no predictor, cache, issue-width change or new execution stage.

For each raw fetched source address, compare in decode against the
current ID/EX rd and current EX/MEM rd, excluding destination zero.
Register the four raw match bits alongside ID/EX advancement: these
producers become EX/MEM and MEM/WB respectively on that same edge.
Reset or an allowed ID flush clears all match bits; genuine ID holds
retain them. Use exactly ID's existing stall/flush priorities, so a
load-use bubble clears matches while dmem or divider holds preserve
the live instruction's cohort. Compare raw source addresses independent
of redirect-derived fetch validity, preserving the prior removal of
redirect feedback from decode and hazard payload paths.

In EX, qualify the registered EX match with the CURRENT EX/MEM
ctrl.reg_write and the registered WB match with the CURRENT MEM/WB
ctrl.reg_write. Then preserve the existing EX/MEM-over-MEM/WB-over-
stored-operand priority and 00/01/10 selector encodings. Do not latch
reg_write prematurely: current controls already reflect branch/jump
and memory alignment traps and divider bubbles. Do not gate MEM/WB
forwarding with valid or WB w_en: a dmem stall clears valid but retains
data, destination and reg_write for forwarding to held EX consumers.
No destination equality comparison remains on the EX forwarding path.

Implement x1 through x31 as generated, individually declared 32-bit
flip-flop registers with constant per-word write destinations and
decoded write enables. Tie x0 to zero and select both combinational
read ports from the register outputs. Keep deterministic synchronous
reset and both existing same-cycle write-first bypasses. Avoid a
dynamically written memory array that Gowin can map into BRAM and
combine with the operand latches; keep ID/EX's existing operand flops
and hold behavior. This storage mapping removes the competing BRAM
output delay that otherwise caps the retimed forwarding network.
The additional flip-flops are the area cost of this same operand-path
optimization; no architectural register state or read latency changes.

Preserve the existing encoded operand muxes, shared signed 33-bit
multiplier, real divider, exact ALTOPS expressions, decoder defaults,
traps, bus readiness, redirects, load-use protection, and nret=1 ports.
During a divide, retain the existing exactly-once operand/metadata
snapshot; after completion, the incoming instruction's registered
matches must correctly identify the divider result entering EX/MEM.
All RVFI source values, memory effects and retirement orders remain
identical to the champion.

A temporary prototype of precisely these changes passed all 21
existing pipeline cases and all five register-file cases. Vendor
placement options 0/1/2 measured 59.887/60.076/60.076 MHz, median
60.076 MHz, 9.31 percent above 54.96 MHz. Option 0 increased from a
reproduced champion 52.491 MHz to 59.887 MHz. Area is 3303 LUTs,
1613 flip-flops, four BSRAMs and two DSPs versus 2499 LUTs, 678
flip-flops, six BSRAMs and two DSPs. Its option-0 worst path starts
at a registered WB match and is 21.993 ns. Retiming alone reached
only 55.117 MHz median, confirming the competing register-file path
must also be addressed. The canonical real-arithmetic CoreMark run
with --bench --istall --dstall completed with no out-of-bounds access,
all five expected CRCs and the required success literal. Its start
and stop markers were 15884 and 4507701: exactly 4491817 marked cycles,
unchanged from the champion. Combined with the measured median Fmax,
this projects fitness 133.7454, a 9.31 percent gain. These are temporary
prototype measurements; full formal and retirement-by-retirement
reference cosim have not been run and remain implementation gates.

Forecast a 9 percent fitness gain at unchanged marked cycles. Routing
from the extra register storage and match alignment during unusual
holds are the main risks. With 4491817 marked cycles, the acceptance
margin requires median Fmax above 57.48816 MHz and fitness above
127.98856. Run the unchanged formal and retirement-cosim gates and
canonical CoreMark UART/CRC/marker checks; compare measured median
Gowin Fmax times actual marker-bounded iterations/cycle.

title: Separate the load/store address pipeline from ALU writeback
motivation:
The champion scores 122.36 at 54.960 MHz and 4,491,817 marked CoreMark
cycles. Its worst Gowin path starts at MEM/WB destination state and
crosses forwarding, EX, the shared ALU, and EX before reaching data
memory. The existing EX/MEM alu_result register serves two different
purposes: integer-result forwarding/writeback and the memory address.
Every ALU operation, including the shared DSP multiply, therefore feeds
the data-memory address even when no memory instruction is active.
Previous structural attempts delayed redirects or blocked multiplication;
their extra cycles outweighed their clock improvements. A separate LSU
address pipeline can remove general ALU selection from the memory request
path without changing any instruction's latency. LESSONS.md is absent;
the structural history contains no attempt to split these two datapaths.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Give the load/store unit its own effective-address adder and EX/MEM
address register, independent of the general ALU result register.
Compute effective_addr = forwarded_rs1 + sign_extended_immediate
directly, without the AUIPC operand mux, register/immediate operand mux,
ALU operation result mux, jump-link mux, or multiplier/divider result
selection. Keep the shared RV32M multiplier and the iterative divider
on the existing architectural result path. This is one structural
separation of LSU requests from integer writeback, not an additional
pipeline stage or a change to the issue/retirement schedule.

Add a 32-bit lsu_addr field immediately after alu_result in ex_mem_t.
Reset it deterministically, hold it on downstream
dmem backpressure, and capture the effective address when a valid legal
memory instruction actually advances from EX. It may retain the last
request address on non-memory instructions and invalid bubbles; the
interface has no address requirement when both memory enables are zero.
Invalid/busy cycles must still clear all side-effect controls. Prevent
synthesis from reconnecting the LSU register's D input to the generic
alu_result bus: its only arithmetic input is forwarded_rs1 + immediate.
Preserve the normal ALU result bus for register writeback and existing
EX/MEM forwarding, including JAL/JALR links and real/ALTOPS arithmetic.
Concretely, initialize normal_payload.lsu_addr from reg_q.lsu_addr and
override it with rs1 + in.imm only when in.valid, !in.ctrl.is_illegal,
and (in.ctrl.mem_read || in.ctrl.mem_write) are all true. After the
aggregate EX/MEM assignment in real divider-wait and divider-completion
arms, explicitly retain reg_q.lsu_addr. All other field assignments and
the downstream hold priorities stay as in the champion.

Drive dmem_addr exclusively from the registered LSU address. Use that
same address for byte-lane selection, load extraction, memory-alignment
faults, and word-aligned RVFI mem_addr. Store data, load data, byte masks,
memory ordering, and exactly-once ready/enable handshakes retain their
existing behavior. Forwarding priority remains youngest ALU writer over
MEM/WB; load-use still inserts exactly one bubble. A previous multiply or
divide that produces a load/store base must reach this dedicated adder
through the same architectural forwarding paths. Retaining an idle
address must never retain a read/write enable or suppress a valid new
request. Divider metadata/result transfers are non-memory operations
and must not overwrite a pending LSU request.

The intent is to remove mode-dependent ALU arithmetic and result
selection from the registered data-memory request path and reduce its
physical fanout, while preserving single-cycle ordinary execution,
branch recovery timing, and the existing marked CoreMark cycle count.
Multiplication still computes and writes fully correct register results;
only its unnecessary connection to the external memory-address register
is removed. Keep the exact nret=1 top-level ports and channel-0 retirement
ordering, decoder default-illegal discipline, all alignment traps,
canonical CRCs and UART validation, and every evaluator file unchanged.

21 existing pipeline tests and both execute-stage integration tests.
Gowin placement options 0/1/2 measured 57.416/58.164/58.164 MHz, with
median 58.164 MHz versus the champion's 54.960 MHz, a 5.83 percent gain.
Option 0 used 2478 LUTs and 710 registers versus the champion's 2499
LUTs and 678 registers, retaining two DSPs. Its worst path ended at
the ALU-result register instead of data memory: 22.711 ns and 13 cells
versus the champion's recorded 24.345 ns and 16 cells. Multiplication
remains on the new worst path, so this is a bounded timing improvement.

2K/-O3/10-iteration run with both approximately 22 percent bus stalls,
all required CRCs, UART success literal, timing markers, and no OOB
accesses. Its marked cycles were exactly 4,491,817, unchanged from the
champion. The measured median Fmax times iterations/cycle is 129.4888

title: Validate cached next-PC predictions after the EX/MEM boundary
motivation:
The current champion reaches 122.36 iterations/second at 54.96 MHz and
takes 4491817 marked CoreMark cycles. Prior predictors reached roughly
4200000 cycles, but their 45.8-46.0 MHz clocks erased that benefit.
The tagged predictor exposed an EX-to-IF-to-ID recovery feedback path;
the direction-only predictor still lost clock rate. Registering every
taken redirect by itself increased cycles to 4850577, despite improving
Fmax on its parent. Prediction makes that extra recovery stage payable
only on mistakes instead of on every taken control transfer. No
LESSONS.md is present; all three earlier predictor attempts and the
registered-redirect attempt were reviewed in experiments/log.jsonl.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Implement one compact PC-only next-PC predictor whose misprediction
recovery is registered at EX/MEM. Use a 32-entry direct-mapped tagged
branch target table, indexed by fetch PC[6:2], with full remaining PC
tags, aligned targets, a conditional/unconditional bit and two-bit
saturating conditional counters. Conditional hits predict taken from
the counter MSB; JAL/JALR entries predict their last resolved target.
Misses predict PC+4. Reset valid bits only; do not reset invalid table
payload arrays. Initialize replacements weakly toward their outcome.
Prediction depends only on the registered fetch PC, never on imem
decoding, forwarded operands, or an EX combinational recovery signal.

Carry the exact selected predicted_next_pc with every accepted fetch
through IF/ID, ID/EX and EX/MEM. Resolve architectural branch direction,
target, alignment faults, jump links and pc_next in EX using the existing
forwarded operands. Register both the selected prediction and actual
pc_next alongside that instruction at EX/MEM. Perform their full-width
equality comparison ONLY after this register, in MEM. Both comparator
data inputs must come directly from EX/MEM flops; do not compute an EX
target-match bit or EX mismatch flag. This puts a register between
forwarded target arithmetic and prediction validation. A stale taken
prediction on an ordinary, illegal or faulting instruction is repaired
to its registered architectural PC+4. Do not add instruction-memory
target additions or target-match logic to ID.

Apply recovery solely from a valid advancing EX/MEM instruction whose
two registered successors differ. A correct
prediction causes no squash, including for taken branches and jumps.
A mistake redirects to the recorded actual successor and squashes both
younger instructions: fetched/decoded state and the current EX result.
Force a side-effect-free EX/MEM bubble for the squashed younger EX
instruction; the older resolving instruction advances and retires once.
Recovery must override imem stalls, load-use stalls and younger divider
holds. Gate divider launch, completion consumption and execute_hold
with the EX squash so a wrong-path DIV/REM cannot launch, delay repair
or leak a result. Preserve the real and ALTOPS division paths.

Train only from an instruction validly advancing through the registered
resolution boundary, never from the younger instruction being squashed
by an older repair. Train both conditional outcomes exactly once, learn
legal aligned JAL/JALR targets, refresh indirect targets, and invalidate
a matching stale entry for non-control or faulting instructions. For
conditional branches store the branch destination PC+imm independently
of the resolved direction; never overwrite it with PC+4 on not-taken
training. Retain
instruction prediction metadata unchanged through all holds. Advance
the fetch PC to its prediction only when imem is ready and ID accepts
that instruction. Preserve dmem freeze priority and MEM/WB forwarding
data retention; a branch held behind an older memory request cannot
recover or train until it advances. Gate MEM recovery and training by
valid and actual MEM advancement, including dmem readiness for memory
instructions. This also covers a stale taken prediction on a load or
store: complete the older memory request once before repairing, and
suppress every younger side effect. Do not assume all repairing
instructions are branches or lack a data-memory request.

Keep raw imem instruction and register addresses independent of repair,
flush and fetch validity. Only separate validity and control state are
squashed; wide ID payload fields and prediction metadata have ordinary
reset/hold enables. Preserve nret=1, every top-level port, all decoder
and trap rules, architectural RVFI source values and successors,
contiguous retirement orders, and all evaluator files and checks.

A fresh reference-ISS replay of the canonical ELF between MMIO markers
found 357527 taken control transfers and 73619 next-PC misses for the
proposed 32-entry table. Charging two bubbles per miss estimates
4281528 cycles versus 4491817 today, a 4.91 percent rate gain before
clock changes. A 64-entry table estimated 4259392 cycles, only about
0.52 percent better despite twice the storage, so select 32 entries.
The reference run produced all five canonical CRCs, the validation
literal and no out-of-bounds access. These are software replay results,
not cycle-accurate RTL measurements: stalls, delayed training and
speculative fetches can change the measured cycle count.

Forecast a 9 percent fitness gain with medium confidence, requiring
roughly 57.1 MHz at the replay cycle estimate. Incorrect predictions
pay one extra recovery cycle, but correct predictions retain zero
bubbles. Unlike earlier designs, EX target arithmetic and comparisons
cannot feed fetch control without crossing EX/MEM. The main uncertainty
is residual table/PC-selection delay and placement on the shared-DSP
champion. At the estimated cycles, the 4.6 percent acceptance margin
requires about 54.80 MHz, nearly the present 54.96 MHz. Evaluate median
Gowin Fmax times marked iterations/cycle; require fitness above 127.99.

title: Feed the shared multiplier directly from forwarded register operands
motivation:
The champion scores 133.75 at median Gowin Fmax 60.076 MHz and
4,491,817 marked CoreMark cycles. Its worst path starts at a registered
forwarding match and crosses EX and the shared multiplier. The real
multiplier currently consumes the general ALU operands: forwarded rs1
passes through the AUIPC PC mux, and forwarded rs2 passes through the
register/immediate mux, before reaching the DSP multiplier. Every legal
multiply uses register operands, so these mode muxes unnecessarily add
logic and routing to its input paths. LESSONS.md is absent. Prior
micro_opt attempts shared the multiplier and registered dependencies;
none bypassed the general ALU mode muxes for multiplication.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Make one local operand-routing optimization: feed the existing shared
real multiplier directly from the fully forwarded rs1 and rs2 words,
while retaining the selected alu_a/alu_b inputs for ordinary ALU work.
All MUL/MULH/MULHU/MULHSU instructions use these register operands.
This removes the AUIPC-PC and register/immediate selection levels from
multiplier inputs without changing any arithmetic unit, pipeline
stage, execution latency, instruction schedule or forwarding priority.

Add two internal 32-bit alu module inputs named mul_rs1 and mul_rs2.
In ex_stage, connect them to the existing post-forwarding rs1 and rs2
signals. Keep .a(alu_a) and .b(alu_b), and keep both existing operand
mode muxes for RV32I arithmetic, AUIPC and address generation. Do not
connect the new ports to in.rs1_val/in.rs2_val: multiplication must
consume the newest fully forwarded architectural source values.

In the real multiplication branch of alu.sv, retain the existing
signedness control definitions, one signed 33-by-33 product, and low/
high-half selection. Change only the operand construction to
mul_a = $signed({a_signed && mul_rs1[31], mul_rs1}) and
mul_b = $signed({b_signed && mul_rs2[31], mul_rs2}).
The original 32 register bits feed the common multiplier directly;
only the extension bit carries operation-dependent signedness.
MUL still uses the low 32 product bits; all three high-half operations
still share bits [63:32]. Introduce no second multiplier, serial sign
correction, DSP primitive, extra operand register or multiply hold.

Keep every exact RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS expression using the existing a/b
interface. The legal M-op decoder already sets is_auipc=0 and alu_src=0,
making selected and raw forwarded operands identical for these
instructions. Preserve actual RV32M bit results and real-formal support.
Keep the blocking divider and its operand/metadata snapshot unchanged.
Branches, JALR, stores and RVFI source snapshots continue using the same
forwarded rs1/rs2. Preserve current-control forwarding qualification,
youngest-writer priority, x0 exclusion, retained-WB forwarding during
dmem stalls, reset, alignment traps, decoder default-illegal discipline,
nret=1 ports and contiguous channel-0 retirement order.

An isolated prototype of exactly these routing changes passed the
existing ALU, pipeline and execute-stage integration suites. All prior
arithmetic vectors and pipeline assertions were retained; ALU stimulus
additionally drove mul_rs1/mul_rs2 with the same operands as a/b.
Gowin placement options 0/1/2 measured 63.878/67.824/67.824 MHz,
giving median 67.824 MHz versus the champion's 60.076 MHz. Matching
option 0 improved 6.66 percent from 59.887 MHz. Its worst arrival
shortened from 21.993 ns to 20.950 ns, with 12 cells in both cases.
Area was 3331 LUTs versus 3303, with unchanged 1613 registers, four
BSRAMs and two DSPs.

The prototype's canonical 2K/-O3/10-iteration CoreMark run with both
approximately 22 percent bus stalls completed without OOB accesses.
The unchanged UART validator accepted all five expected CRCs and the
required success literal. Start/stop markers were 15884/4507701,
exactly 4,491,817 marked cycles, unchanged from the champion. Combining
these cycles with measured median Fmax projects fitness 150.9946,
a 12.89 percent gain over 133.75. These prototype measurements do not
replace the orchestrator's full formal and retirement-reference cosim
gates, which remain required without weakening any invariant.

Forecast a rounded 13 percent fitness gain. Synthesis may merge the
multiplier inputs back into the general ALU operand network, and WB
mux or result-selection routing can become the next timing limit.
Ensure the synthesized multiplier operands exclude PC/immediate mode
muxes. Judge actual median vendor Fmax times measured marker-bounded
iterations/cycle; acceptance requires fitness above 139.9025, about
62.84 MHz if the marked cycle count remains unchanged. Preserve every
evaluator file and correctness check.

title: Move multiplication into MEM with dependency-only interlocks
motivation:
The champion scores 133.75 iter/sec at 60.076 MHz and 4,491,817 marked
CoreMark cycles. Its worst path starts at a registered forwarding match and
traverses EX operand selection and the ALU. The structural history shows
that a blocking partial-product multiplier added about 282,000 cycles while
improving Fmax only modestly; separate LSU addressing also failed to beat
the newer champion. A later multiply result should break forwarding-to-
multiplier timing without charging every multiply several extra execution
cycles. No LESSONS.md exists; all structural log entries were reviewed
before selecting this proposal.

hypothesis.motivation:
The champion scores 133.75 iter/sec at 60.076 MHz and 4,491,817 marked
CoreMark cycles. Its worst path starts at a registered forwarding match and
traverses EX operand selection and the ALU. The structural history shows
that a blocking partial-product multiplier added about 282,000 cycles while
improving Fmax only modestly; separate LSU addressing also failed to beat
the newer champion. A later multiply result should break forwarding-to-
multiplier timing without charging every multiply several extra execution
cycles. No LESSONS.md exists; all structural log entries were reviewed
before selecting this proposal.
hypothesis.hypothesis:
Retiming the shared multiplier into the existing MEM stage will improve
fitness by removing forwarded operand selection from its input path. Keep
single issue, the existing stage count and nret=1. Execute ordinary RV32I
operations and branch resolution in EX as today, but treat
MUL/MULH/MULHU/MULHSU as late-result producers, analogous to loads. This is
one structural change to multiplication's execution boundary.

At normal EX advancement, register the fully forwarded rs1 and rs2 in the
existing EX/MEM operand fields, together with alu_op and instruction
metadata. Those fields are already required for architectural RVFI values;
use them as hardware multiplier operands. Compute one shared signedness-
selectable 33-by-33 product from these registered operands in MEM,
preserving the champion's shared-product formulation. MUL uses the low 32
bits; the three high-half operations select bits 63:32 with the correct
operand extension signs. Register the selected product as MEM/WB.alu_result,
leaving load data and ordinary EX results on their existing paths. Do not
add a blocking multiply state machine, extra arithmetic stages, separate
partial-product trees, or an EX multiply bypass. Independent instructions
continue to issue each cycle, and multiplication and an adjacent load/store
can occupy successive stages.

Generalize the existing readiness-qualified load-use detector to cover a
valid legal multiply in ID/EX. The prototype changes only core wiring: feed
id_ex_w.ctrl.mem_read OR id_ex_mul to the hazard unit's existing
id_ex_mem_read input; no hazard_unit port or algorithm change is needed. If
the next accepted instruction names its nonzero destination, hold the fetch
PC and insert one ID/EX control bubble, exactly as for a load. Conservative
raw source comparisons are acceptable initially. Exclude multiply producers
from EX/MEM forwarding by driving the existing forward_unit ex_mem_w_en with
ex_mem_w.ctrl.reg_write AND NOT ex_mem_mul; do not change its registered
matching or qualify held WB forwarding by MEM/WB.valid. No EX-stage edit is
needed: normal_payload already captures forwarded rs1_val and rs2_val. Their
result is not ready in EX/MEM. A dependent consumer advances one cycle later
and obtains the final product through existing MEM/WB forwarding. Preserve
youngest-writer priority, x0 behavior, registered dependency alignment, and
the held MEM/WB data used during dmem stalls. Do not route the combinational
MEM product directly to EX; that would recreate the multiplier-to-
forwarding-to-ALU path this proposal is intended to break.

Remove real multiplication hardware from the ordinary EX ALU result cone.
Give standalone multiplier arithmetic a small combinational module so tests
retain all four operations' exact vectors. Under ALTOPS this late module
implements the same exact algebraic MUL-family constants, using the captured
source values; keep the same late-result interlock schedule in formal and
real builds. Preserve the existing DIV/REM iterative unit and its ALTOPS
substitutions. Retain decoder default illegal, alignment traps, all memory-
side ports, channel-0 RVFI values and contiguous orders, and all existing
evaluation checks and files.

Downstream dmem backpressure still holds EX/MEM and ID/EX, and clears
MEM/WB.valid while retaining its data. A multiply waiting behind an older
memory operation must keep its forwarded operands correct until it can
advance; after advancement its captured operands remain stable. A delayed
product must retire and write back once. Existing divider bubbles must not
erase a multiply result still needed by a held divide; divider launch must
capture that result through normal WB forwarding. Preserve redirects and all
wrong-path side-effect suppression.

Forecast a 16 percent fitness gain with medium confidence, from higher Fmax
and at most one extra cycle per immediate multiply dependency. The earlier
experiment estimated 93,960 marked MULs, giving a nominal worst-case extra
93,960 cycles, about 2.09 percent, if every MUL needs that bubble. Bus-stall
overlap and random-sequence alignment can change this estimate. At 4,585,777
cycles, beating 133.75 by 4.6 percent needs approximately 64.16 MHz; with no
extra cycles it needs 62.84 MHz. The principal risk is the standalone
multiplier still setting Fmax, or the new MEM result selection becoming
critical. Compare the complete median Gowin Fmax times marker-bounded
iterations/cycle, and require fitness above 139.9025 iter/sec.

An isolated prototype of this exact retiming measured Gowin placement
options 0/1/2 at 65.713/70.072/70.072 MHz, median 70.072 MHz, versus 60.076
MHz for the champion. Its canonical 2K/-O3/10-iteration CoreMark run with
both bus stalls took 4,527,646 marked cycles, only 0.80 percent more than
the champion, and passed the unmodified validator for all five CRCs, the
success literal, timing markers and no OOB accesses. The measured product is
154.76475 iter/sec, 15.71 percent above 133.75 and above the 139.9025
acceptance threshold. Placement option 0 used 3352 LUTs and 1657 registers,
versus 3303 and 1613 currently, and two DSPs. Its worst reported path was
20.512 ns, 13 cells; the multiplier no longer appeared on that worst path.

All 53 generated checks from the unchanged single-channel formal config
passed with ALTOPS in a private staging tree; real and ALTOPS multiplier
vector suites passed; selftest retirement cosim passed both zero-wait and
with both stalls. All 27 prototype pipeline tests passed, including added
MUL-to-DIV, retained WB product under a long store stall, JALR, younger-
writer priority and x0 checks. Existing selectors/cycle-gap assertions tied
to immediate EX multiplication were changed to assert the specific intended
WB source and single dependency bubble, retaining all operand, arithmetic,
retirement, trap and memory checks. These prototype results substantiate the
rounded 16 percent forecast; the orchestrator must still reproduce the
implementation and run every normal correctness and fitness gate.

changes.description:
Add a combinational shared signedness-selectable 33-by-33 multiplier.
Use a_signed for MULH/MULHSU and b_signed for MULH, with each signed
33-bit operand equal to {signed_mode AND operand[31], operand}.
Compute one signed 66-bit product; select [31:0] for MUL and [63:32]
for high-half operations. Include the exact unchanged four MUL-family
ALTOPS formulas. Pipeline registers remain in EX/MEM and MEM/WB.

Instantiate the late multiplier using in.rs1_val, in.rs2_val and
in.ctrl.alu_op. Define is_mul as in.valid AND NOT in.ctrl.is_illegal
AND the four MUL-family op matches. Capture MEM/WB.alu_result from

title: Instruction-validated direct-target prediction with narrow EX recovery
motivation:
The champion scores 133.75 at 60.076 MHz with 4491817 marked CoreMark
cycles. Earlier tagged predictors reached about 4197500 cycles, but
their recovery logic lowered Fmax; the instruction-derived target
predictor also lost clock rate. Registered next-PC verification took
4281035 cycles and reached only 52.294 MHz on its older parent. There
is no LESSONS.md; all recorded predictor attempts were reviewed.
The opportunity is to remove recurring direct-control bubbles while
avoiding both an imem-to-PC target adder and an EX target comparison.

hypothesis.motivation:
The champion scores 133.75 at 60.076 MHz with 4491817 marked CoreMark
cycles. Earlier tagged predictors reached about 4197500 cycles, but
their recovery logic lowered Fmax; the instruction-derived target
predictor also lost clock rate. Registered next-PC verification took
4281035 cycles and reached only 52.294 MHz on its older parent. There
is no LESSONS.md; all recorded predictor attempts were reviewed.
The opportunity is to remove recurring direct-control bubbles while
avoiding both an imem-to-PC target adder and an EX target comparison.
hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add one 32-entry direct-mapped instruction-validated direct-target
predictor to the current champion. Each entry contains a valid bit,
the full remaining PC tag, the exact 32-bit instruction word, an
aligned PC-relative target, and a two-bit direction counter. Index
with fetch PC[6:2]. Cache only legal aligned conditional branches
and JAL instructions; leave JALR on the existing resolve-and-redirect
path. Reset valid bits, initialize replacement counters weakly toward
the observed outcome, and train both branch outcomes exactly once.
A JAL hit always predicts taken; a conditional hit uses counter MSB.
Misses and instruction mismatches predict fall-through. Do not add
global history, a return stack, or a different pipeline depth.

Require BOTH the PC tag and the stored instruction word to match the
raw current imem instruction before using a cached target. The target
was computed for that exact PC/instruction pair on a prior legal,
aligned resolution. Consequently an accepted direct taken prediction
already has the correct destination. Changing instruction memory,
PC-index aliases and illegal encodings cannot reuse a wrong target.
Keep all PC bits in the tag, including non-index low bits if needed;
do not silently rely on a restricted code address range. The lookup
target comes only from storage: no B/J immediate addition on the
prediction-to-PC path. Compare raw instruction bits independently of
redirect, readiness and validity, and qualify only the narrow select.
Evaluate PC-tag equality and instruction equality in parallel, then
combine their Boolean results with valid/type/direction in the final
target select. Write an entry's PC, instruction and destination
coherently on allocation so a lookup cannot mix different versions.

Carry only predicted_taken with each fetched instruction into ID/EX.
For direct control transfers EX uses the existing authoritative
target arithmetic, operand forwarding and alignment rules. Its
recovery condition is predicted_taken XOR actual_taken, where
actual_taken means a legal aligned taken branch or JAL. No full-width
predicted-target/actual-target comparator or predicted_next_pc bus is
required. JALR stays unpredicted and redirects to its actual aligned
target as today. Include a defensive recovery to PC+4 for unexpected
predicted_taken on a non-direct or faulting instruction. An accepted
recovery squashes the younger fetch; a correctly predicted direct
transfer lets its ready target instruction enter ID/EX that cycle.
Architectural pc_next, trap behavior, JAL/JALR links and RVFI fields
always come from the normal resolution path, never the predictor.

Define resolve_fire as a valid instruction actually advancing from
EX to EX/MEM. Gate training and recovery by resolve_fire, excluding
dmem freezes and unfinished divider operations. Retain prediction
metadata across genuine holds. Advance predicted PC only when imem
is ready and ID accepts the fetch; recovery overrides imem and
load-use holds after older memory stalls permit EX advancement.
Preserve divider handshakes and saved metadata, MEM/WB retained
forwarding data, load-use bubbles and exactly-once retirement.
Store the conditional destination PC+imm even on a not-taken update;
never train a destination with the fall-through successor. Replace
the entry when PC or instruction differs, initializing its own
counter rather than inheriting unrelated hysteresis. Ignore bubbles,
faulting controls and JALR in training.

Preserve the champion's registered forwarding comparisons and
individually declared flop register file. Preserve separation of
wide ID payload reset/hold logic from flush-controlled valid/ctrl.
Prediction metadata uses the payload capture enable; redirect must
not feed operand, instruction or register-address muxes. Implement
the small table without resetting its invalid payload arrays and
inspect Gowin mapping; instruction/tag checks and target selection
are the main new timing risk. Keep ordinary ALU and divider unchanged.

A fresh reference-ISS replay of the canonical ELF between its MMIO
markers recorded 2922016 instructions and 357527 taken control
transfers, including 13735 JALR transfers deliberately unpredicted
here. The proposed 32-entry direct cache produced 71195 direct
direction misses and a net 272597 one-cycle bubbles saved. Charging
these against the champion gives an estimated 4219220 cycles and
a 6.46 percent rate gain at unchanged clock. A 16-entry table saved
257288 bubbles; 64 entries saved 283121, only 0.25 percent better
estimated throughput than 32 despite doubled storage. Select 32
entries. The replay produced all five canonical CRCs, ITERATIONS=10,
the validation literal and no out-of-bounds accesses. These are
software prediction statistics, not an RTL performance or correctness
result: speculative fetches, training latency and bus-stall overlap
can change the actual cycle count.

Forecast a 6 percent fitness improvement with medium confidence.
At the replay estimate the 4.6 percent acceptance margin requires
about 59.03 MHz versus the champion's 60.076 MHz. The timing budget
is therefore tight; avoiding fetch addition and wide EX validation
is essential, and the new instruction equality/lookup cone remains
the main uncertainty. Measure median Gowin Fmax times marked
CoreMark iterations/cycle and require fitness above 139.9025.
Preserve nret=1, all top-level ports and all formal, cosim, canonical
CRC/UART, bounds and marker requirements.

through wb_stage and EX forwarding into the shared multiplier, and

by shortening this same arithmetic cone. Moving multiplication to MEM
reached only 149.41 because its new dependency bubbles cost cycles.
No LESSONS.md exists; the recorded micro_opt attempts were reviewed.
The remaining WB load-versus-ALU mux is an avoidable level ahead of
forwarding and multiplication, even though both candidate values are
already available before the MEM/WB edge.
