title: Carry-inferred micro-BTB target validation in parallel with branch resolution
motivation:
The champion scores 150.99 at 67.824 MHz and 4491817 marked CoreMark
cycles. Earlier predictors removed roughly 290000 cycles but lost
clock rate; registered MEM recovery reduced that cycle benefit.
The latest instruction-validated target cache timed out on formal
pc_fwd rather than establishing correctness. LESSONS.md is absent.
The opportunity is a small predictor whose target correctness is
checked explicitly without an adder followed by an equality reduction.
This addresses the earlier timing and proof problems together.

hypothesis.motivation:
The champion scores 150.99 at 67.824 MHz and 4491817 marked CoreMark
cycles. Earlier predictors removed roughly 290000 cycles but lost
clock rate; registered MEM recovery reduced that cycle benefit.
The latest instruction-validated target cache timed out on formal
pc_fwd rather than establishing correctness. LESSONS.md is absent.
The opportunity is a small predictor whose target correctness is
checked explicitly without an adder followed by an equality reduction.
This addresses the earlier timing and proof problems together.
hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add one 16-entry direct-mapped micro-BTB to the current champion,
indexed by fetch PC[5:2]. Each entry holds a full remaining PC tag,
an aligned full-width target, valid and conditional/unconditional
type bits, and a two-bit saturating conditional direction counter.
Predict conditional branches from the counter MSB and JAL from their
cached target; misses predict PC+4. Leave JALR unpredicted. Allocate
a new entry only after a legal aligned taken direct transfer; initialize
a conditional counter weakly taken. On a tag hit, train both branch
outcomes and saturate the counter. A not-taken miss does not evict an
existing useful target. Reset valid bits only.

Implement each entry as an independently declared register bank with
constant-index writes. Decode the fetch index into one-hot enables,
compare that entry's complete PC tag locally, and gate its target
by its valid, tag-hit and taken state. OR the mutually exclusive
target terms with a balanced tree. Avoid a priority encoder, a
dynamically indexed packed target array, and instruction-memory
validation on the prediction-to-PC path. Full tags, including any
non-index low PC bits, must distinguish every architectural PC.
This deliberately small lookup is the predictor's timing hypothesis.

Carry predicted_taken and the exact selected target with each accepted
fetch into ID/EX. In EX, validate the untrusted cached direct target
with a parallel addition checker instead of calculating an addition
and then comparing its output. Let P be the original instruction PC,
D its correctly sign-extended B/J immediate, and T the captured cached
target. Use exactly 32-bit unsigned vectors and modulo-2^32 arithmetic:
C = ((P & D) | ((P ^ D) & ~T)) << 1;
target_match = ((P ^ D ^ T ^ C) == 32'b0).
C[0] is zero and overflow beyond bit 31 is discarded. Each inferred
carry depends only on the preceding operand/target bits; no carry
propagates through the checker. A balanced zero reduction checks
every bit. This identity is true iff T equals P+D, for arbitrary
32-bit operands and arbitrary cached targets. An independent Yosys
SAT proof of that equivalence passed during hypothesis generation.

Feed the checker only from the held ID/EX PC, immediate and captured
target. Compute it in parallel with forwarded branch comparison and
the existing architectural target adder. It must not depend on that
adder's output, instruction-memory data, a forwarded register operand
or a previous table write. Keep target addition in EX for recovery
addresses and RVFI exactly as today. Do not add an ID target adder,
an ID target comparison, full instruction-word tags, or a MEM recovery
stage. Predictor state need not satisfy a remembered-target invariant
for architectural correctness: an arbitrary wrong target is detected
locally before any younger instruction can acquire side effects.

Resolve conditional direction in EX with the existing forwarded
operands. A direct branch or JAL recovers on a direction mismatch
or a taken prediction whose parallel target_match is false.
JALR always uses the existing resolve-and-redirect path, including
when a stale PC-tagged direct entry predicted that PC taken.
Unexpected taken predictions on ordinary, illegal or faulting
instructions recover to architectural PC+4. Correctly predicted
transfers admit the target fetch without a bubble. Preserve all
alignment traps, architectural successors and original PC+4 links.

Qualify training and recovery by resolve_fire: the valid instruction
actually advancing from EX to EX/MEM, excluding older dmem stalls
and unfinished division. Never repeatedly train or redirect a held
branch. Carry prediction metadata through genuine holds, including
the divider's held instruction. Recovery overrides imem and load-use
stalls once older memory permits advancement.
PC follows a prediction only when imem is ready and ID accepts the
corresponding instruction. Bubbles clear all side-effect controls.

For existing conditional hits, retain/update the true branch destination
on both outcomes; never replace it with fall-through. Ignore JALR in allocation,
initialize replacement state, and invalidate a matching stale entry
when a non-control or faulting instruction resolves. Keep raw imem
bits and register addresses independent of prediction recovery.
New wide ID payloads have ordinary reset/hold logic, while flush
only clears the existing separate validity/control registers.

Keep the champion's forwarded-register multiplier inputs, registered
forwarding matches, flop register file, iterative divider, MEM/WB
forwarding retention, pipeline depth, nret=1 and all top-level ports.
Do not change arithmetic, decoder legality or evaluation contracts.
Compared with earlier 32/64-entry predictors, trade modest prediction
coverage for shallow selection and substantially smaller symbolic
state. Unlike the earlier full-word cache, explicit target checks
remove its remembered-target invariant from pc_fwd correctness.
Unlike the earlier target-comparison predictor, the checker neither
follows an adder nor lengthens the imem-to-ID payload path.
No formal assumptions may constrain instructions, predictor state
or memory to make this proposal pass.

A fresh reference-ISS replay of the canonical ELF between MMIO markers
recorded 2922016 instructions and 357527 taken control transfers,
including 13735 unpredicted JALR transfers. The chosen 16-entry direct
table with taken-only allocation had 67510 direct successor misses
and saved a net 276282 bubbles. Charging one cycle per net bubble
gives 4215535 estimated cycles and a 6.554 percent rate gain at
unchanged clock. Allocating on both branch outcomes instead saved
257288 bubbles: avoiding not-taken miss allocation saves a further
18994 cycles with no additional table bits. The chosen 16-entry table
also slightly exceeds the earlier 32-entry allocate-both-outcomes
replay's 272597 saved bubbles despite having half as many entries.
With the same taken-only policy, 32 entries saved 289623 bubbles,
only 13341 more than 16 entries, about 0.32 percent extra throughput
at unchanged clock. Retain 16 entries to favor timing and proof size.
The replay produced all five canonical CRCs, ITERATIONS=10, the
validation literal and no out-of-bounds access. These are software
statistics, not cycle-accurate RTL measurements: speculative fetches,
update latency and overlap with bus stalls can change the cycle count.

Forecast a 6 percent fitness gain with low confidence. The gain must
come from fewer marked CoreMark cycles without a material median
Gowin Fmax loss. Require measured fitness above 157.93554, the
champion plus the 4.6 percent acceptance margin. At the replay cycle
estimate, median Gowin Fmax must exceed about 66.578 MHz versus the
current 67.824 MHz, so the timing budget remains tight. The predictor
lookup and the parallel checker/recovery reduction are the main
timing risks. Preserve all formal, cosim, canonical
CRC/UART, memory bounds and marker checks; this is an unmeasured
architectural hypothesis, not a reported RTL result.

title: Bypass the generic ALU result mux for effective memory addresses
motivation:
The current champion scores 173.20 at median Gowin Fmax 78.418 MHz
and 4527646 marked CoreMark cycles. Its worst path crosses forwarded
operand selection and the EX ALU before reaching data memory.
LESSONS.md is absent. Earlier micro_opt wins shortened operand/result
delivery; the latest accepted change moved multiplication to MEM.
The remaining dmem address is nevertheless sourced from the complete
generic ALU result, including shifts, comparisons and bitwise operations
that can never generate a legal load/store address. This unnecessarily
puts the wide ALU result-selection cone on the memory address path.

hypothesis.motivation:
The current champion scores 173.20 at median Gowin Fmax 78.418 MHz
and 4527646 marked CoreMark cycles. Its worst path crosses forwarded
operand selection and the EX ALU before reaching data memory.
LESSONS.md is absent. Earlier micro_opt wins shortened operand/result
delivery; the latest accepted change moved multiplication to MEM.
The remaining dmem address is nevertheless sourced from the complete
generic ALU result, including shifts, comparisons and bitwise operations
that can never generate a legal load/store address. This unnecessarily
puts the wide ALU result-selection cone on the memory address path.
hypothesis.hypothesis:
Make one local datapath-routing optimization: give EX/MEM a dedicated
registered effective_addr = fully forwarded rs1 + decoded immediate,
and drive every memory address-dependent function from that field.
Keep address computation in the existing EX stage and capture it on
the same edge as the current EX/MEM payload. Add no stage, latency,
predictor, cache, scheduling change or arithmetic algorithm change.

In ex_stage, compute the 32-bit modulo-2^32 sum directly from rs1
after the existing forwarding mux and in.imm. Bypass the AUIPC-PC mux,
register-versus-immediate mux, general ALU operation/result mux and
JAL-link result selection for this effective-address lane. Do not
use stale in.rs1_val or truncate address width. Retain the generic
alu_result path for register arithmetic, links, division and early
forwarding. Capture effective_addr into the existing normal_payload
with the identical reset and downstream-hold behavior as EX/MEM.
Divider metadata and bubble construction must still initialize and
carry the complete bundle; the added field has no memory side effects
unless the existing legal load/store controls request an access.

In mem_stage, replace all address uses of in.alu_result with
in.effective_addr: dmem_addr, byte-lane position, load extraction,
word/halfword alignment detection and the RVFI aligned mem_addr.
Leave architectural wb_result selection using in.alu_result for
ordinary ALU results; it must not select effective_addr instead.
Retain store replication, load sign extension, access-enable gating,
alignment trap behavior and ctrl.reg_write suppression exactly.
Keep hold_wb's retained data and controls with valid-only clearing,
current-control forwarding priority, multiply dependency bubbles,
divider handshakes and snapshots, decoder default-illegal discipline,
nret=1 ports and contiguous channel-0 retirement order.

For every legal load/store, the original ALU has ALU_ADD, alu_src=1
and is_auipc=0, so the dedicated sum is exactly the original effective
byte address for all 32-bit operands. For other instructions the dmem
address pins may carry this sum while both memory enables stay zero;
no memory transaction or architectural result changes. This is normal
separation of address generation from general register-result routing,
including in deployments with synchronous FPGA memory. It removes
irrelevant ALU functions from a real memory interface and allows
shorter memory input setup paths, without changing the evaluation
wrapper or relying on address range restrictions.

An isolated prototype of exactly this added field, direct EX sum and
MEM address-use substitutions passed all 33 existing real-arithmetic
pipeline cases and the existing ALTOPS pipeline case. Gowin placement
options 0/1/2 measured 77.049/83.484/83.484 MHz, giving median 83.484
MHz, 6.46 percent above the champion's 78.418 MHz. Area was 3386 LUTs
and 1690 registers versus 3306 and 1626, with unchanged four BSRAMs
and two DSPs. The option-0 worst path shifted from ALU-to-memory
addressing to WB-through-redirect/decode control, confirming that
the original memory-address bottleneck was removed. Its arrival
shortened from 18.433 ns to 18.273 ns; placement options 1/2 had
17.273 ns worst arrival. The new control path limits further gains.

The canonical 2K/-O3/10-iteration CoreMark binary on the prototype
with both approximately 22 percent bus stalls completed at EBREAK,
with no out-of-bounds accesses. The unchanged UART validator accepted
all five expected CRCs and the required validation literal. Start and
stop markers were 15915 and 4543561, exactly 4527646 marked cycles,
unchanged from the champion. Combining measured median Fmax with
those cycles projects fitness 184.3872, a 6.46 percent improvement.
These isolated timing and benchmark measurements are not a completed
formal or retirement-reference cosim evaluation; those gates remain
required during implementation. Prototype RTL is temporary and is
not part of the submitted source change.

Forecast a rounded 6 percent fitness gain with medium confidence,
entirely through Fmax at unchanged marked cycles. Adding the 32-bit
sum/register increases area and exposes redirect/decode as the next
limit. The acceptance margin is modest: preserve this exact routing
change and avoid unrelated mux or control rewrites. Acceptance
requires fitness above 181.1672 and approximately 82.025 MHz median
Fmax at 4527646 marked cycles. Run existing arithmetic, pipeline,
formal and retirement-cosim gates and canonical CoreMark
CRC/UART/bounds/marker checks without weakening any invariant.

title: Split fixed immediate shifts from a registered late barrel-shift lane
motivation:
The champion scores 173.20 iter/sec at 78.418 MHz with 4,527,646 marked
CoreMark cycles. Its worst path starts at a registered forwarding match
and crosses EX operand selection and the ALU before reaching data memory.
The successful r6s1 structural change moved multiplication behind a
registered operand boundary while retaining early ordinary-ALU forwarding
and unified registered WB completion. The remaining five-level barrel
shifter is a promising next execution unit to isolate. LESSONS.md is absent;
all six prior structural attempts were examined, and none split shift
execution. Blocking execution and uniformly delayed redirects previously
lost enough cycles to cancel their clock gains.

A reference-ISS replay of the canonical marked workload found 274,353
shifts, all immediate forms. Shifts by one or two account for 117,700 of
these and 42,660 adjacent raw-source dependencies. Their computation can
use fixed bit wiring and a small one-versus-two mux, avoiding the general
five-bit shift network. Preserving that early path limits the cycle cost
of moving the general barrel shifter into MEM.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Split shift execution into an early fixed-immediate path and a registered
late barrel-shift completion lane. This is one structural change to the
shift execution boundary: SLLI/SRLI/SRAI with amounts exactly 1 or 2 remain
single-cycle EX results; every other immediate shift and every register
SLL/SRL/SRA becomes a late MEM result. Preserve the stage count, single
issue, EX branch resolution, nret=1, and the current retirement boundary.
Do not add a blocking shift state machine or general MEM-to-EX shift bypass.

In ID, register two payload bits alongside the normal operands:
shift_early = dec_alu_src && (dec_alu_op is SLL/SRL/SRA) &&
              (instruction[24:20] equals 1 or 2);
shift_two = (instruction[24:20] equals 2).
Use the validated decoder outputs, so register forms, illegal encodings
and all non-shift instructions cannot acquire early shift eligibility.
Reset and hold these bits with the ID/EX payload, independently of flush;
the existing separate controls and valid bit keep bubbles inert. No
forwarded value, redirect or imem-ready signal enters this classification.

In EX, implement only the early fixed shifts with concatenations:
left-by-one {rs1[30:0],1'b0}; left-by-two {rs1[29:0],2'b0};
right-by-one {fill,rs1[31:1]}; right-by-two {{2{fill}},rs1[31:2]}.
Here rs1 is the fully forwarded operand and fill is rs1[31] only for SRA,
otherwise zero. shift_two selects the fixed amount; the already registered
alu_op selects left versus right and logical versus arithmetic fill.
Select this result when shift_early is set, ahead of the existing jump-link
and ordinary ALU result selection. There must be no variable-shift operator
on this early path. Set an elaboration-time ENABLE_SHIFTS parameter on alu
(default true for its existing standalone suite) to false in EX, returning
zero for its three shift cases there. Keep all other ALU operations and
exact M-extension ALTOPS constants unchanged. The synthesized EX instance
must contain no general barrel shifter.

Add shift_late and five-bit shift_amount to EX/MEM. Capture shift_amount
from alu_b[4:0], which already correctly chooses immediate versus forwarded
rs2. Capture shift_late as a shift-operation match AND NOT shift_early.
Reuse the existing captured fully forwarded rs1_val as the MEM shifter data;
preserve rs2_val separately as the architectural RVFI source value even for
immediate shifts. Hold this metadata with the existing downstream dmem
freeze. Normal bubbles clear controls/readiness and are side-effect-free.

Instantiate a small combinational shifter in MEM from registered rs1_val,
shift_amount and alu_op, with exact SLL/SRL/signed-SRA semantics for amounts
0 through 31. Qualify shift completion with in.valid, !in.ctrl.is_illegal,
and in.shift_late. Select the completed shift before the unified WB register:
in.ctrl.mem_to_reg ? load_data : is_mul ? mul_result :
is_shift ? shift_result : in.alu_result.
Early fixed shifts follow the ordinary in.alu_result path. WB still drives
registered wb_result directly, without a post-register completion mux.
The general barrel shifter and forwarding operand mux therefore occupy
different clock paths.

Register fwd_ready false for late shifts as well as existing loads and
multiplies; retain readiness for early fixed shifts. Concretely extend the
existing EX expression with NOT(!in.shift_early && shift_op_match), preserving
ctrl_with_trap.reg_write, load/multiply exclusion and divider completion.
Extend the existing valid-legal late-producer interlock in core with
id_ex_shift = id_ex_w.valid && !id_ex_w.ctrl.is_illegal &&
              !id_ex_w.shift_early && shift_op_match.
Feed mem_read OR id_ex_mul OR id_ex_shift to the existing hazard input.
Keep readiness-qualified raw source comparisons, x0 exclusion and all
hazard priorities unchanged. An immediately dependent late-shift consumer
gets exactly one bubble and receives the result from registered WB;
early shifts retain EX/MEM forwarding with no new bubble. Independent
instructions and consecutive independent late shifts still issue every
clock. Do not decode shift readiness from MEM combinationally.

Preserve youngest-writer priority, registered dependency alignment,
write-first register reads, and MEM/WB data retention during dmem holds.
WB forwarding remains usable after valid clears; register writes remain
valid-qualified. A shift blocked behind older memory advances exactly
once, and its completion retires once. Shift-to-store, branch, JALR,
MUL and DIV dependencies must use correct forwarded architectural values.
Divider requests still snapshot operands before older sources drain.
Wrong-path operations never reach side effects. Retain all decoder,
alignment-trap, memory-order, reset, RVFI-source and contiguous-order rules.
Use this identical early/late shift schedule under RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS:
only M-extension arithmetic receives its existing substitutes.

An isolated prototype of exactly the specified amounts and boundaries
measured Gowin placement options 0/1/2 at 83.566/85.865/85.865 MHz, median
85.865 MHz, versus the champion's 78.418 MHz. Option 0 used 3368 LUTs,
1640 registers, four BSRAMs and two DSPs. Its worst path was 17.261 ns,
versus the recorded champion's 18.433 ns. The canonical 2K/-O3/ten-iteration
CoreMark simulation with both approximately 22 percent bus stalls took
4,611,078 marker-bounded cycles, 1.843 percent more than the champion.
The unchanged UART validator accepted all five canonical CRCs and the
success literal; the run reached EBREAK, had both markers and no OOB.
The measured product is 186.21459 iter/sec, 7.514 percent above 173.20
and above the required 181.1672 acceptance threshold. All 53 checks from the unchanged single-channel ALTOPS formal config
passed in private staging, including all six real shift instruction checks,
register causality, PC forwarding/backward consistency, illegal encodings,
order uniqueness and liveness. The existing 28 pipeline cases and both
EX integration cases passed with packed-field/source-list updates, as did
the existing ALTOPS multiply-schedule case. An added directed pipeline
case passed all six shift forms for every amount 0 through 31, with and
without both bus stalls: it checked exact results, architectural source
values, store consumers and contiguous RVFI orders, plus exactly zero new
bubble for immediate shifts by 1/2 and exactly one for all dependent late
shifts in zero-wait mode. Selftest full retirement cosim against the
unchanged ISS passed with both bus stalls (115 retirements).

Forecast a rounded 8 percent fitness gain with medium confidence. These
are isolated prototype measurements, not a substitute for the orchestrator's
implementation, full correctness gates or fitness evaluation. At the
measured cycle count acceptance requires median Fmax above 83.53761 MHz,
giving about 2.33 MHz of margin. The principal risk is another ALU,
redirect or MEM product-selection path limiting timing after replication,
or an implementation changing the early-shift eligibility and cycle cost.
Preserve every evaluator file and every hard invariant, including nret=1
ports, EBREAK-only SYSTEM legality, canonical CRC/UART checks and markers.

title: Compact micro-BTB with registered training and live successor checks
motivation:
The current champion scores 173.20 at 78.418 MHz with 4527646 marked
CoreMark cycles. LESSONS.md is absent. Earlier predictors consistently
removed about 275000 to 294000 cycles, but lost enough clock rate to
miss acceptance. The latest 16-entry carry-checking predictor passed
formal and cosim and reached 4216285 cycles on its older parent, while
the instruction-word-validated cache timed out on formal pc_fwd.
The current champion has since moved multiplication into MEM and
registered early-forwarding eligibility. The promising predictor
opportunity is to preserve that shorter EX result path, register the
predictor-training boundary, and avoid wide prediction metadata.

hypothesis.motivation:
The current champion scores 173.20 at 78.418 MHz with 4527646 marked
CoreMark cycles. LESSONS.md is absent. Earlier predictors consistently
removed about 275000 to 294000 cycles, but lost enough clock rate to
miss acceptance. The latest 16-entry carry-checking predictor passed

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add one 16-entry, direct-mapped, PC-tagged predictor for conditional
branches and JAL only. Use PC[5:2] as the index and a compact ten-bit
tag {PC[13:6], PC[1:0]}, full aligned targets, a valid bit and a two-bit
saturating counter per entry. Every hit uses the counter MSB, including
JAL; a new JAL entry starts weakly taken and repeated JAL outcomes
reinforce taken. No conditional/unconditional type bit is stored.
Misses predict PC+4. Leave JALR unpredicted. Allocate
only after legal aligned taken direct transfers, initialize new
entries weakly taken, and train both outcomes on hits.
Not-taken misses must not evict useful entries. Cache the branch
destination independently of its outcome, never PC+4 on a not-taken
update. Reset valid bits only. Use independent constant-index entry
registers, local one-hot hit qualification and balanced target OR
selection. Lookup uses the registered PC without imem decoding.

Exploit the actual front-end topology: IF/ID is combinational and
ID/EX is the sole instruction register before EX. After a fetch is
accepted into ID/EX, the fetch PC itself holds that instruction's
selected successor. If EX is blocked by an older memory operation or
unfinished division, ID/EX and fetch PC both hold. Therefore EX can
validate the current registered fetch PC instead of carrying a second
32-bit predicted target or predicted_next_pc through ID/EX. Introduce
no wide prediction fields and no predicted_taken field. This is valid
only with accepted-resolution recovery and acceptance-coupled PC
advancement, which are mandatory parts of this hypothesis.

Check direct targets with a combinational inferred-carry identity in
parallel with branch direction, avoiding an adder followed by equality.
For 32-bit unsigned P=ID/EX.pc, D=ID/EX.imm, and T=current fetch PC:
C = ((P & D) | ((P ^ D) & ~T)) << 1;
direct_match = ((P ^ D ^ T ^ C) == 32'b0).
Arithmetic is modulo 2^32 and the shift discards overflow. The same
identity with D=32'd4 gives fallthrough_match. Use a specialized
constant-four implementation if synthesis benefits, preserving exact
full-width equivalence. Both match outputs depend only on registers
and shallow Boolean reductions, never on the architectural target
adder, operand forwarding, current imem bits or remembered-table
correctness. Partial-tag aliases intentionally remain possible for
PCs differing above bit 13; explicit full-width successor checks
repair every wrong selection, including stale hits on non-controls.
No architectural PC or cached target is truncated and no code-location
assumption is permitted. The earlier attempt proved this identity;
retain an explicit independent equivalence check during implementation.

For a legal aligned taken conditional branch or JAL, recover iff
direct_match is false. For ordinary, illegal, faulting or not-taken
instructions, recover iff fallthrough_match is false. Continue to
resolve legal aligned JALR through the existing forwarded target and
unconditional recovery path. Trapping JALR uses fall-through repair.
Drive redirect_target from the SAME authoritative actual pc_next wire
used by normal_payload.pc_next, computed with the existing EX adders
and trap rules. Do not rebuild a second wide recovery-target mux from
actual_direct_taken/actual_jalr. Preserve JAL/JALR
PC+4 link data, architectural RVFI successors and forwarded operands.
A prediction to the actual successor admits the ready fetched
instruction without a bubble. Wrong targets, changed instructions,
table aliases and stale entries on non-controls are repaired locally;
correctness must not depend on a cached-target invariant or on code
immutability. Invalidate a matching stale entry when a non-direct or
faulting instruction resolves.

Define resolve_fire as a valid instruction actually transferring
from EX into EX/MEM, excluding dmem holds and unfinished division.
Gate recovery with resolve_fire. A held branch must neither retrain
nor move the fetch PC. Redirect overrides
imem-not-ready and load-use holds only when EX can advance. Otherwise
update fetch PC to its selected prediction exactly when the fetched
instruction enters ID/EX as valid. An imem bubble, load/multiply-use
bubble, older memory freeze or divider hold never consumes a
prediction. Correct resolutions must not squash the target fetch.
Divider completion participates in fall-through validation on the
result-transfer edge; preserve its captured operands and metadata.
Do not add a fetch queue or another instruction stage: they would
invalidate the live-successor relationship used by the checker.

Train the table one cycle after EX resolution from a compact registered
update record aligned with EX/MEM. Register only update PC[13:0], the
aligned full target[31:2], legal-aligned-direct eligibility, actual
taken outcome and a valid event bit. No instruction word, full PC tag,
conditional type or architectural result belongs in this record.
Qualify training by actual MEM advancement, including dmem readiness
for non-control instructions invalidating stale hits.
The training path must have no combinational dependence on forwarded
operands, the live EX comparator, execute_hold or EX recovery. A
registered taken outcome controls allocation and counter increments.
Keep this small predictor update record separate from div_metadata_q:
division never needs to snapshot predictor targets, tags or counters.
The original PC stays held in ID/EX until DIV completion, so that
result-transfer edge can emit a normal non-direct update record.
Predictor update payloads use ordinary capture/hold logic; their valid
bit is zero during unfinished division and bubbles. Hold the record
with EX/MEM during a downstream freeze and gate table writes with
downstream advancement, avoiding repeated training.
An isolated first probe exposed
forwarded-branch-to-table-write fanout as its worst timing path, so
this registered training boundary is essential, not optional. It
delays learning by one cycle while leaving prediction and EX recovery
latency unchanged. Bubbles and stalled MEM instructions never update.

Preserve the champion's MEM multiplier, unified registered WB value,
registered fwd_ready, registered dependency matches, write-first flop
register file, MEM/WB forwarding retention and late-producer interlock.
Keep recovery out of raw imem data, source-address muxes and wide ID
payload D/enable paths. Only the existing separate valid/control
registers clear on an allowed squash. Preserve nret=1, all top-level
ports, decoder legality, alignment traps, all arithmetic and every
formal/cosim/CRC/UART/bounds/marker requirement.

An isolated prototype of this final sixteen-entry, ten-bit-tag design
measured Gowin placement options 0/1/2 at 77.926/77.325/77.325 MHz,
median 77.325 MHz. Option 0 used 4469 LUTs, 2361 registers, four BSRAMs
and two DSPs; its worst path remained the existing EX ALU to memory,
18.127 ns and 13 cells. The marker-bounded CoreMark run with both
bus stalls took 4251084 cycles and passed the unchanged validator for
all five CRCs, ten iterations and the success literal, with no OOB.
The measured product is 181.89478 iter/sec, a 5.020 percent gain over
173.20 and above the 181.1672 acceptance threshold. This reduces marked
cycles by 276562 while losing 1.39 percent clock rate.

All 53 tasks from the unchanged single-channel ALTOPS formal config
passed in a private staging tree. The final prototype also passed
full retirement-trace cosim for selftest and random1/2/3, each with
zero wait and with both bus stalls. An independent Yosys SAT proof
established the inferred-carry equality for arbitrary 32-bit operands
and for the constant-four case. These are hypothesis-generation probe
results, not a substitute for the implementation phase's gates.

Forecast a rounded 5 percent fitness gain with low confidence because
the acceptance margin is narrow. At 4251084 cycles acceptance requires
median Fmax above 77.01570 MHz, just 0.40 percent below the measured
77.325 MHz. Preserve the exact small table, registered training and
shared architectural successor path. Predictor placement and the
live-PC-check-to-recovery cone are the principal remaining risks.
Measure marked cycles and median vendor Fmax after implementation;
cycle savings alone do not establish success. The design focuses on
one direct predictor and its validation, with no arithmetic, memory,
pipeline-depth, global-history or return-stack changes.

title: Use validity tokens to squash decode and forwarding payloads
motivation:
The current champion scores 184.39 iter/sec at median 83.484 MHz and
4,527,646 marker-bounded CoreMark cycles. LESSONS.md is absent. Structural
history shows that delaying all redirects added 358,760 cycles and that
moving shifts to MEM also lost acceptance; adding execution latency is
therefore unattractive. The champion's detailed Gowin report instead
shows a forwarded WB operand passing through the branch comparator and
redirect logic to a decode reset net that feeds validity and decoded
controls. Clearing the whole decoded control bundle makes branch recovery
a high-fanout pipeline control operation even though one validity bit can
represent the same bubble.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Restructure ID/EX and its dependency matches as independently held
payloads plus a live instruction token. Capture ctrl_decoded on ordinary
payload advancement regardless of fetch availability or squash. Reset the payload normally,
but remove flush and fetch validity from every decoded-control D input,
synchronous reset and clock enable. Only ID/EX.valid is cleared by a
redirect, unavailable fetch or load/multiply-use bubble. Retain the
current payload hold on true dmem/divider holds and the current flush
priority for inserting dependency bubbles. This is one structural change
to bubble representation and side-effect qualification, with no extra
instruction stage or changed arithmetic/branch latency.

Apply the same split to forward_unit's four registered raw dependency
matches. Reset them to zero and update their unchanged source/destination
comparisons only when !stall, but do not clear them on flush. Keep the
existing flush input unused or remove its internal connection; flush must
not enter match-register resets, data inputs or hold enables. On a load-use
bubble, stall is asserted and the raw matches retain their previous
payload; on a redirect without a stall they may capture the wrong-path
payload. These matches are inert because the consuming instruction's
token is invalid. Their current producer readiness qualification remains
authoritative. The next valid consumer still captures matches on the same
edge as its operands and decoded payload, so no latency is added.

Make every consumer of potentially stale decode controls validity-aware.
Feed the hazard unit exactly (id_ex_w.valid && id_ex_w.ctrl.mem_read)
OR the already valid-and-legal id_ex_mul expression. Existing branch/jump
recovery and divider request/hold gates already require a live instruction;
retain them. At the EX/MEM boundary, invalid EX tokens
clear only ctrl_with_trap.reg_write, mem_read and mem_write, giving
fwd_ready=0 through the existing reg_write qualification. Start
ctrl_with_trap from in.ctrl, mask these three side-effect bits when
!in.valid, then retain the existing misalign_fault trap override. Keep
the other decode fields as payload; do not replace this with an
in.valid mux on the whole control bundle. Preserve the architectural
payload and exact trap flags for live instructions. Downstream memory requests and
register writes must still require a live, non-faulting instruction.
Forwarding must never select a stale EX/MEM producer created from an
invalid ID/EX token. Keep the registered dependency-match alignment and
youngest-writer priority. Reset, squash, invalid fetch data and bubbles
cannot launch arithmetic, access memory or create an interlock.

Preserve the special MEM/WB forwarding lifetime during a downstream
hold: clearing retirement valid must not remove the retained producer's
registered result, rd or reg_write eligibility. Do not globally gate
MEM/WB forwarding with retirement valid. Register writes and retirement
remain valid-qualified, so the retained producer never commits twice.
Divider launch snapshots fully forwarded operands before sources drain,
divider wait emits inert EX/MEM bubbles, and pending completion transfers
exactly once. Keep real and ALTOPS multiply schedules and arithmetic,
memory and control-target alignment traps, and nret=1 ports unchanged.

The expected gain comes from disconnecting the late EX comparison and
redirect cone from the decode control bank, reducing its reset fanout
and leaving only the compact live token on that recovery path. Keep
redirect out of raw instruction/source-address paths and all payload
hold enables. No predictor, memory cache, late shifter or arithmetic
redesign is part of this hypothesis. With unchanged marked
cycles, acceptance requires median Gowin Fmax above 87.325587 MHz and
fitness above 192.87194 iter/sec. Verify actual marker-bounded cycles
and all three placement options; the remaining comparator or ALU path
may limit the gain. Preserve every invariant and evaluator-side file.

An isolated prototype with exactly this decode-payload, raw-match and
three-side-effect-bit structure measured Gowin placement options 0/1/2
at 86.299/88.326/88.326 MHz, median 88.326 MHz. Option 0 used 3370 LUTs,
1692 registers, four BSRAMs and two DSPs. Its worst path was 16.882 ns
and 12 cells from WB through the ordinary EX ALU, compared with the
champion's 18.273 ns and 38-cell redirect/control path. The canonical
2K/-O3/ten-iteration run with both bus stalls took exactly 4,527,646
marked cycles, unchanged, and passed the unchanged UART validator for
all five CRCs, success literal and ten iterations; both timing markers
were present, EBREAK was reached and no OOB occurred. The measured
product is 195.08151 iter/sec, 5.798 percent above 184.39.

All 53 tasks generated by the unchanged single-channel ALTOPS formal
configuration passed in private staging. All eight full retirement
cosim runs passed: selftest and random1/2/3, each with zero wait and
both bus stalls. All 36 existing pipeline cases passed after replacing
only the physical-zero ID-control-bubble assertion with explicit
effective-side-effect checks: an invalid token cannot redirect, launch
DIV, hold execution, create a late-producer hazard, write memory or
registers, or become an early producer. Preserve the existing holds,
transaction counts, expected architectural results, RVFI values and
ordering assertions. All five existing execute integration cases and a
new invalid-control case passed, covering stale ALU/load/store/branch/
JAL/JALR/MUL/DIV payloads with no effect. These probe results do not replace the
implementation phase's required correctness and fitness gates.

Forecast a rounded 6 percent fitness gain with low confidence because
the measured clock margin over acceptance is only 1.0004 MHz, or
1.146 percent. Both removing decode squashes and removing match squashes
are essential: retaining the match-register flush measured only
86.705 MHz median and missed acceptance. Keep this precise topology
rather than adding broader validity gating to the forwarding network
or changing the arithmetic, branch comparator or instruction schedule.

title: Sixteen-entry direction prediction with narrow parallel recovery
motivation:
The champion scores 184.39 iter/sec at 83.484 MHz and 4527646 marked
CoreMark cycles. LESSONS.md is absent. Predictor attempts r6s2 and
r7s2 passed correctness and removed roughly six percent of cycles,
but their target tables and validation logic lost enough Fmax to
miss acceptance. The earlier r3s2 direction-only predictor reached
4203461 cycles and passed formal/cosim; its worst path was ordinary
EX arithmetic on a substantially older core. Revisit that direction
predictor on the current early/late-result core, with a much smaller
metadata footprint, registered training, and explicit short fetch
target arithmetic. The main opportunity is zero-bubble direct
transfers without a remembered-target correctness check in EX.

The champion scores 184.39 iter/sec at 83.484 MHz and 4527646 marked
CoreMark cycles. LESSONS.md is absent. Predictor attempts r6s2 and

but their target tables and validation logic lost enough Fmax to

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add one 16-entry PC-indexed bimodal direction predictor, using
PC[5:2] and two-bit saturating counters initialized weakly not taken.
Consult it only for a positively validated BRANCH encoding. Predict
legal aligned JAL instructions taken immediately. Leave JALR on the
existing forwarded resolution path. Every predicted target is computed
from that exact raw fetched instruction and its full original PC;
table aliases affect direction accuracy only. There are no target
entries, tags, valid bits, instruction-word caches, global history,
return stack or indirect predictor.

Extract B and J offsets directly from raw imem bits, independently of
recovery and fetch validity. Use a split-carry direct-target datapath
rather than a serial full-width fetch adder. For a branch, compute
{carry,low12} = {1'b0,PC[11:0]} + {1'b0,Bimm[11:0]}.
Compute PC[31:12]+1 and PC[31:12]-1 in parallel. The target high20
is unchanged when carry equals Bimm[31], incremented for a positive
offset with carry, or decremented for a negative offset without carry.
For JAL apply the same construction with low20, carry20 and high12,
using Jimm[31] as the sign. Keep every architectural PC bit and discard
only overflow beyond bit 31: these are exact modulo-2^32 sums, including
page crossings and wraparound. Branch and JAL low additions and upper
increment/decrement candidates run in parallel; only narrow carry/sign
selects follow them. Verify each identity independently against full
addition. Retain the ordinary PC+4 lane. Require a word-aligned target
before taking any prediction; reserved branch funct3 values predict
fall-through. Do not add recovery-dependent instruction masking.

Carry only the actual selected predicted_taken bit in if_id_t and
id_ex_t. No predicted target, predicted_next_pc, registered direct
target or fall-through bus is added to the pipeline. EX retains the
existing architectural PC+imm and PC+4 calculations for trap handling,
links and RVFI. Since the prediction target was computed from the
very same captured PC/instruction, direct recovery needs only a
direction-bit mismatch for a legal aligned conditional branch. JALR
remains unpredicted and recovers to its actual aligned target. Aligned
JAL is always correctly predicted, so it needs no EX repair condition.
Ordinary and illegal instructions always select fall-through. Predict
a faulting direct target not taken, and preserve architectural
fall-through on its trap. Enforce the local relationship between
captured instruction and selected prediction; arbitrary direction
counter values cannot violate it. Do not compare live fetch PC against PC+imm or
PC+4, and do not introduce a carry-inferred successor checker or rely
on stored-target invariants.

Make predictor recovery deliberately parallel. Compare the forwarded
operands in four eight-bit lanes, computing less-than and equality in
each lane simultaneously. Unsigned less-than is lt3 OR (eq3 AND lt2)
OR (eq3 AND eq2 AND lt1) OR (eq3 AND eq2 AND eq1 AND lt0); signed
less-than selects rs1[31] when the operand signs differ and otherwise
uses that unsigned result. Equality is the AND of lane equalities.
Select equality, signed-less or unsigned-less by branch_op[2:1].
Architectural branch_cond XORs this base with branch_op[0]; recovery
XORs it with the early, register-only polarity
(branch_op[0] XOR predicted_taken). This short comparison replaces
a full-word carry-dependent comparison in the predictor recovery
path, without changing the meaning of any of the six branch opcodes.
Reuse the same operand predicates for resolved architectural direction.

Preselect the direct recovery destination from the captured prediction
bit: a taken prediction that proves wrong repairs to original PC+4;
a fall-through prediction that proves wrong repairs to original
PC+imm. JALR selects its normal forwarded jump_target. The late branch
comparison therefore controls only the repair event, never a second
wide target mux before IF's recovery mux. Architectural pc_next still
follows actual branch_cond, jump and trap rules for RVFI. On every
accepted recovery prove that this preselected redirect_target equals
the architectural successor. The only repair sources are
(is_branch AND aligned_direct_target AND branch_mismatch) OR
(is_jalr AND NOT misalign_fault), qualified by valid EX advancement.
Decode already positively validates these controls. Do not add generic
non-control successor repair logic: this predictor stores no targets
or control types, and fetch qualification guarantees predicted_taken=0
for every non-direct instruction. Check this implication locally and
retain all ordinary instruction, illegal and alignment formal gates.
Do not share a late actual-direction target mux into timed recovery.

Predicted PC advancement must coincide exactly with valid ID/EX
acceptance. Load/multiply-use bubbles, imem-not-ready, older dmem
freezes and divider holds do not consume a prediction. Hold the
prediction bit with its instruction using ordinary payload reset/hold
logic; ignore it when invalid. A correctly predicted direct transfer
admits a ready target fetch without squashing it. Gate recovery with
a valid EX instruction actually advancing to EX/MEM, excluding dmem
freezes and unfinished division. Accepted repair overrides imem and
load-use holds. Divider result transfer participates in normal
fall-through resolution, while preserving its saved operands/results.

Train direction counters from a small separate EX/MEM-aligned record:
four-bit branch index, one-bit actual outcome, and a valid event bit.
Capture only legal aligned conditional branches on EX advancement;
hold the record with EX/MEM and clear its event on bubbles/divider
waits. Consume it once on MEM advancement. No full PC, target, decoded
instruction or predictor state enters div_metadata_q. Thus forwarded
branch comparison drives only local update flops, never distributed
table writes in the same cycle. Use constant-index counter registers,
local write enables and balanced direction selection, avoiding a
priority encoder and coherent-target allocation logic. Train both
outcomes with saturation; jumps, traps and repeated holds never train.

Preserve the champion's effective-address bypass, MEM multiplier,
unified registered WB result, registered early-forward eligibility
and dependency matches, flop register file, load/multiply interlock,
retained MEM/WB forwarding under dmem stalls, and blocking divider.
Keep raw imem data, source-address comparisons and wide ID operand
payloads independent of recovery. Keep nret=1 and all IO, retirement,
legality, alignment, arithmetic and evaluation invariants unchanged.

Forecast five percent fitness improvement with low confidence.
An isolated prototype of this exact sixteen-entry architecture measured
placement options 0/1/2 at 78.680/82.761/82.761 MHz, median 82.761 MHz.
Option 0 used 3617 LUTs, 1729 registers, four BSRAMs and two DSPs;
its worst path was the existing forwarded EX ALU, not fetch target
generation. At this clock acceptance above 192.87194 iter/sec requires
fewer than approximately 4291000 marked cycles. The implementation
phase must rerun canonical CoreMark, all correctness gates and median
vendor timing; narrow recovery and small state are essential to the
clock budget. The acceptance margin is narrow, and physical routing
remains the main uncertainty.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Make one combinational resource-sharing optimization in alu.sv. Form enable_ab = (op == ALU_AND || op == ALU_OR) and enable_axorb = (op == ALU_OR || op == ALU_XOR). Compute the 32-bit lane logic_result = ((a & b) & {32{enable_ab}}) | ((a ^ b) & {32{enable_axorb}}). Replace the three separate result arms with exactly one grouped ALU_AND, ALU_OR, ALU_XOR arm returning logic_result. The two operand bits and two enable bits give a four-input Boolean function per result bit. AND enables only the common-one term, XOR enables only the differing-bit term, and OR enables both disjoint terms. Keep the existing exact opcode case to select this lane, so all other opcodes and the zero default retain their current behavior. Add no ALU input mux, register, extra stage or vendor primitive.

Preserve every other ALU operation, including the champion's exact five-level shared SRL/SRA network, independent SLL, ADD/SUB, SLT/SLTU, LUI and all eight exact ALTOPS formulas. Keep the selected a/b inputs, fully forwarded architectural operands, early-result eligibility, pipeline latencies, hazard schedule and branch penalty unchanged. Keep multiply/divide arithmetic, traps, decoder default-illegal discipline, memory handshakes, WB retention after valid clears, redirect-over-stall priority, nret=1 ports, RVFI sources/results and contiguous retirement order. Modify no evaluator files or invariant checks.

An isolated prototype of this exact grouped lane measured placement option 1 at 90.954 MHz with 3297 LUTs, 1690 registers, four BSRAMs and two DSPs, versus champion option 1 at 90.490 MHz and 3348 LUTs. Its worst arrival was 16.289 ns. This 0.51 percent clock gain is below acceptance and is not a completed fitness measurement. Two equivalent control formulations and the XOR merge of the disjoint terms are being checked to select a single better Boolean-lane implementation; the final file will specify only the chosen one. Forecast a five percent fitness improvement with low confidence. Routing and the competing redirect path may cap gains. Require the unchanged formal, unit, retirement-cosim and canonical CoreMark CRC/UART/bounds/marker gates, and all three vendor placement options. At unchanged 4,527,646 cycles acceptance requires median Fmax above 94.652 MHz and fitness strictly above 209.05356. Do not treat the preliminary result as an accepted improvement.

title: Split operand resolution and arithmetic into separate execution stages
motivation:
The champion reaches 199.86 iter/sec at 90.490 MHz with 4,527,646
marker-bounded CoreMark cycles. LESSONS.md is absent. Structural r2s1
delayed redirects and r7s1 delayed shifts; neither improved fitness
enough. Structural r8s1 removed decode squashes but reached only
88.326 MHz. The successful MEM multiplication and unified registered
WB result are already present. The remaining bottleneck combines
forwarded operand selection with arithmetic or branch comparison.
Isolated source-comparison-bank and forwarding-control probes on this
champion failed to improve timing; the best reached 85.363 MHz and
still reported a WB-to-EX ALU path. A stronger register boundary is
needed to separate operand delivery from computation.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add one execution pipeline register between operand resolution and
arithmetic. Replace the current combined EX stage with EX1, which
reads the integer register file and selects completed producer values,
followed by EX2, which executes exclusively from captured operands.
The topology is fetch/decode -> EX1 operand resolution -> EX2 execution
-> MEM completion -> WB retirement. Preserve single issue and nret=1.
This is one pipeline-depth change, not a collection of independent
arithmetic, predictor or memory optimizations.

Keep the existing decode instruction register as the EX1 input buffer.
It carries PC, instruction, immediate, source/destination addresses,
validated controls and a live token. Move register-file read addressing
to that buffered instruction. Read current register values in EX1,
rather than retaining old operand values through a dependency stall.
Keep x0 and the existing write-first WB bypass. In EX1, choose the
youngest available registered EX/MEM ordinary result, then registered
MEM/WB wb_result, then current register-file data. Capture both resolved
architectural source values with the complete instruction metadata in
the new EX1/EX2 register. No ALU, barrel shift, branch comparison,
address addition or JALR target arithmetic precedes this register.

EX2 contains the current base ALU, target/link calculations, alignment
checks and blocking divider launch/completion logic. Its only operand
inputs are the new register's rs1_val and rs2_val; eliminate the EX2
forwarding muxes entirely. Keep the dedicated effective-address lane,
EX/MEM result and readiness register, existing MEM multiplier and load
extraction, unified WB register and retirement boundary. Multiplication
consumes EX2's captured operands through the existing EX/MEM fields.
DIV/REM requests snapshot these operands and metadata exactly once.
Keep real RV32M arithmetic and all exact ALTOPS substitutions.

A producer still executing in EX2 has no registered result available to
EX1. If the buffered consumer needs its nonzero destination, hold that
consumer and fetch, let the producer advance, and inject a side-effect-
free bubble into EX1/EX2. A load or multiply in EX/MEM is also unavailable
until registered WB completion: hold dependent EX1 consumers for the
extra cycle. Thus immediate ALU dependencies normally gain one bubble;
immediate load/multiply dependencies normally need two rather than one.
Independent instructions still issue every clock. Use validated source
usage for operand readiness, distinguishing register arithmetic, OP-IMM,
loads, stores, branches and JALR from instructions without those sources.
Preserve the architectural convention for RVFI source-address/data fields:
readiness checks must also cover any raw source value the unchanged
cosim contract expects to observe, even when that value is semantically
unused. Do not silently substitute arbitrary RVFI source values to avoid
an interlock. Prefer conservative raw-source stalls when necessary.

For each source, an unavailable younger matching writer blocks issue
even if an older EX/MEM or WB writer of the same register is available.
Exclude x0 producers. Use current registered fwd_ready and WB write
eligibility, including alignment-trap suppression. Treat invalid pipeline
tokens as inert and preserve effective reg_write/memory controls on all
bubbles. Re-reading the register file while EX1 waits captures writes
from producers that have already drained; do not rely on stale decoded
operand snapshots or a WB source whose instruction has moved away.

Data-memory backpressure freezes EX/MEM and EX1/EX2 plus the buffered
consumer and fetch. MEM/WB clears only retirement valid and retains its
producer data and eligibility, as today. Captured EX2 operands remain
stable through the complete hold; they no longer depend on a forwarding
source surviving that hold. Unfinished division holds EX2 and upstream
while older MEM/WB instructions drain once. Division wait emits inert
EX/MEM bubbles; completion transfers the saved result once and releases
EX2 on that edge. A dependent EX1 instruction cannot capture the divide
result until the registered producer is available. Preserve reset
cancellation, result backpressure and the current ALTOPS execution rules.

Resolve branches and jumps in EX2, retaining full-width architectural
targets, JAL/JALR links, all branch predicates and alignment traps.
Compared with the champion, accepted taken transfers gain one recovery
bubble. On a valid EX2 redirect actually advancing past older memory,
redirect fetch and squash both younger buffered instructions: decode/EX1
and EX1/EX2. Suppress EX1 capture on that edge, including younger stores,
branches and DIV/REM requests. The redirecting EX2 instruction advances
normally and retires once. Preserve accepted redirect priority over
instruction-memory unavailability and dependency bubbles; never drop a
target, repeatedly consume a held branch, or squash the older memory op.
Keep recovery out of wide operand payload D muxes: clear the new live
token and all effective side-effect controls while payloads may capture
irrelevant data. No speculation or predictor is added.

Preserve every core port and the nret=1 channel-0 retirement convention,
strictly contiguous RVFI orders, decoder default-illegal and EBREAK-only
SYSTEM legality, memory and target traps, memory ordering, all five
canonical CoreMark CRCs, UART success text, markers and OOB enforcement.
Modify only target RTL and allowed cocotb suites. Do not change formal
depths, ALTOPS formulas, evaluator files or the declared retirement width.

Forecast twelve percent fitness improvement with low confidence. The
new architecture is not implemented or measured in this research turn;
the preceding probes are negative evidence, not its timing results.
The intended benefit is a substantially faster clock because register-
file/forwarding and ALU/branch logic occupy different clock paths. The
principal risk is added dependency and control-flow bubbles outweighing
that clock gain, or register-file/MEM logic limiting the new clock.
At 120 MHz acceptance above 209.05356 iter/sec requires fewer than
approximately 5,740,156 marked cycles; at 135 MHz it requires fewer than
6,457,675 cycles. These are tradeoff bounds, not predicted measurements.
A twelve percent gain would need about 6.03 million cycles at 135 MHz.
Require the unchanged formal suite and full retirement cosim, canonical
CoreMark validation and all three Gowin placement options. Accept only
the measured Fmax times marker-bounded iterations/cycle, exceeding the
champion by 4.6 percent; do not judge pipeline depth or Fmax alone.

title: Opcode-biased stateless direct prediction with narrow recovery
motivation:
The current champion takes 4527646 marked CoreMark cycles at 90.49 MHz.
LESSONS.md is absent. Prior target-table predictors consistently lost
clock speed; the r8s2 sixteen-entry direction predictor passed formal
and cosim and reduced cycles to 4254282, but its 83.849 MHz median
produced only 197.09 iter/sec. A predictor needs to protect the clock
and exceed 209.05356 iter/sec to clear the current acceptance margin.
Use static opcode/loop bias to eliminate table state, lookup multiplexers,
branch-update fanout and training registers from the prediction cone.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Implement one stateless opcode-biased predictor for positively
validated conditional branches: BEQ predicts not taken, BNE predicts
taken, and BLT/BGE/BLTU/BGEU predict backward taken and forward not
taken. For valid branch funct3 values the direction is exactly
instr[14] ? instr[31] : instr[12], a three-input Boolean function.
Also predict legal aligned JAL taken. Leave JALR on its existing
forwarded resolution path. No branch PC, benchmark address, operand,
mutable history or software annotation selects the static policy.
Extract B/J immediates from
raw imem data, calculate their exact full-width modulo-2^32 targets,
and predict taken only if that target is word-aligned. Reserved branch
funct3 values and all non-direct instructions select PC+4. Store no
tags, target entries, counters, validity arrays or training metadata.

Carry only the actual selected predicted_taken bit through if_id_t
and id_ex_t. Keep prediction decode and all wide payloads independent
of redirect, flush and fetch validity. Capture this bit with the
ordinary instruction payload, holding it through true pipeline holds.
Advance fetch PC to the selected successor precisely when that same
instruction enters ID/EX as valid; imem stalls, load/multiply-use
bubbles, older dmem freezes and divider waits consume no prediction.

Use exact split-carry B/J target generation to bound fetch delay:
branch low12 addition and JAL low20 addition run beside upper-PC
increment/decrement candidates, followed by carry/sign selection.
Keep all architectural address bits, correctly handle crossings and
wraparound, and reject misaligned targets. Verify this construction
against ordinary 32-bit addition before relying on it. Preserve the
independent PC+4 lane and original PC+4 link results.

EX still computes architectural branch direction, targets, alignment
traps and RVFI pc_next from captured instruction/PC and forwarded
operands. Since every predicted direct target was computed from that
exact instruction, aligned conditional recovery requires only actual
direction XOR predicted_taken. Correctly predicted JAL needs no
recovery; aligned JALR retains unconditional EX recovery. Preselect
the conditional recovery destination from predicted_taken: PC+4 if a
taken prediction was wrong, PC+imm otherwise. Actual branch comparison
must not select a second wide target mux in the timed recovery path.
Preserve fall-through and suppressed link writes on alignment traps.
No remembered-target or generic full-width successor check is needed.
Enforce locally that a selected prediction is a legal aligned direct
transfer and that every recovery target equals architectural pc_next.

Qualify recovery with a valid EX instruction actually advancing into
EX/MEM, excluding downstream freezes and unfinished division. A held
branch cannot repeatedly move PC. Accepted recovery overrides imem
stalls and load-use holds; a correct prediction admits the ready target
fetch without squashing it. Preserve existing hazard/forwarding rules,
MEM/WB producer retention during dmem stalls, divider request/result
handshakes, effective-address bypass and MEM multiplication. Do not
introduce predictor state into divider metadata or alter arithmetic.

The hypothesis is that loop-biased static prediction removes enough
direct-transfer bubbles while retaining substantially more of the
champion's Fmax than dynamic table predictors. Measure canonical
CoreMark cycles and median Gowin Fmax together; lower cycles alone do
not establish improvement. Keep nret=1, all external ports, decoder
legality, exact RVFI successors/orders, and every existing correctness,
CRC, UART, MMIO-marker and memory-bound check unchanged.

title: Parallel EX result banks with direct one-hot producer bypass
motivation:
The champion scores 199.86 iter/sec at 90.490 MHz and 4,527,646
marker-bounded CoreMark cycles. LESSONS.md is absent. Structural r9s1
split operand resolution from execution, reaching 103.173 MHz but
increasing cycles to 5,518,993 and reducing fitness to 186.94. Structural
r7s1 delayed most shifts into MEM and also missed acceptance. Adding
dependency latency is therefore expensive. A fresh unchanged-champion
Gowin option-0 report shows a 16.797 ns path from an ID operand through
forwarding, the AUIPC operand mux, right shifting and six subsequent
selection cells into EX/MEM. Its 16.793 ns companion starts at a
forwarding-match register. The shift result should cross a register
before joining other operation results, without delaying its availability.
An isolated first banked prototype with a common bank-selection mux
reached only 82.029 MHz; flattening its four-source operand network
recovered 90.470 MHz. These are negative probes, not a successful
candidate. Their limiting path starts at the registered bank kind and
crosses binary forwarding selection. The proposed direct per-bank
eligibility removes that serial control topology.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace the single mixed EX result register with parallel registered
shift and ordinary-integer completion banks at the same EX/MEM boundary.
Move the shift-versus-integer result selection AFTER that boundary.
This is one structural retiming of result selection, with the existing
single-issue pipeline, early forwarding latency and nret=1 retained.

Keep ADD/SUB, comparisons, Boolean operations, LUI/AUIPC, jump links and
completed division on the existing ordinary-result register. Remove
variable shifts from that register's combinational ALU result cone.
Compute SLL/SRL/SRA in a dedicated combinational lane from fully forwarded
rs1 and the existing immediate-or-forwarded-rs2 shift amount. Bypass the
AUIPC operand-A mux: shifts always use architectural rs1. Preserve the
champion's explicit five-level shared SRL/SRA network and exact signed
fill; implement SLL with its own exact variable-shift network.

Capture the dedicated shift result in its own 32-bit bank on every
!stall_ex_mem edge, with synchronous reset. Its data and update enable
must not depend on jump-link selection, divider busy/completion, flush,
instruction validity, or operation-result selection. Bubbles and nonshift
instructions may capture irrelevant bank data; effective controls and
registered per-bank eligibility keep it inert. Hold the bank during
genuine downstream memory freezes. Register shift-result eligibility with
the instruction at EX/MEM and clear it for reset and divider-wait bubbles;
DIV completion selects the ordinary-result bank. Keep the ordinary bank's
existing divider metadata/result and trap behavior.

Add mutually exclusive registered fwd_int_ready and fwd_shift_ready bits
alongside the two EX/MEM banks. Derive them before the register from the
existing fwd_ready expression AND NOT shift_kind or AND shift_kind,
respectively. A legal early producer has exactly one ready bank; loads,
multiplies, bubbles and faulting register writers have neither. Completed
division uses the ordinary ready bank from its captured metadata.

Forward_unit must directly emit four one-hot source enables per operand:
saved ID/EX value, registered EX/MEM integer bank, registered EX/MEM shift
bank, or registered MEM/WB result. Reuse the existing ID-aligned raw
match registers. For source s, define early_match = ex_match_s AND
(fwd_int_ready OR fwd_shift_ready), wb_match = wb_match_s AND retained
MEM/WB reg_write. Integer and shift enables are ex_match_s AND their
respective registered ready bits. WB enable is NOT early_match AND
wb_match; saved-operand enable is NOT early_match AND NOT wb_match.
This guarantees youngest-producer priority and exactly one enabled input.
Merge four masked 32-bit buses in a balanced OR network in EX. Do not
encode these enables into a binary selector and decode them again; do
not multiplex the two EX/MEM banks before operand forwarding; do not
use a bank-kind bit to qualify an already encoded generic EX bypass.

Keep a registered shift_kind for MEM completion only. In MEM, select
the registered shift or integer bank for ordinary/shift WB completion,
behind the existing load and multiplication selection.
WB remains the unified registered wb_result. Shift instructions stay
early fwd_ready producers: add no shift-use interlock, blocking engine,
MEM shifter, extra pipeline stage or combinational MEM arithmetic bypass.
Independent and immediately dependent shifts keep their current schedule.

Preserve registered dependency matches, EX/MEM-over-WB priority, x0,
write-first reads, and retained MEM/WB forwarding during memory holds.
Architectural RVFI operands remain the original fully forwarded sources,
never shifted substitutes. Stores, branches, JALR, multiply and division
consuming shift results must receive the selected architectural value.
Keep dedicated LSU addressing, real and ALTOPS multiplication, all DIV
substitutions, divider handshakes and exactly-once retirement intact.
Use the same shift banking in real and ALTOPS builds.

Forecast an unmeasured eight percent fitness improvement with low
confidence. At unchanged cycles, acceptance above 209.05356 iter/sec
requires median Gowin Fmax above 94.65254 MHz. The expected saving is
removal of the generic ALU/result-selection tree after the barrel
shifter together with direct one-hot bank forwarding. This direct
per-bank version is distinct from the two unsuccessful timing probes.
A branch recovery path is already nearly tied with the shift path;
this or the added bypass mux can limit the gain. Require all three Gowin
placement options and actual marker-bounded cycles before accepting.
Preserve every hard invariant, core port, decoder legality, alignment

title: Remove AUIPC operand selection from the ordinary EX datapath
motivation:
The champion scores 199.86 iter/sec at 90.490 MHz and 4,527,646
marker-bounded CoreMark cycles. LESSONS.md is absent. Prior micro_opt
attempts improved timing by bypassing irrelevant operand selection
for multiplication (r5s0) and effective addresses (r7s0). The recent
Boolean-lane change gained only 0.51 percent, below acceptance.
Splitting execution increased dependency cycles, and parallel result
banking reduced Fmax. The remaining ordinary ALU still receives rs1
through a 32-bit AUIPC-versus-register mux before every arithmetic,
comparison and shift operation. Only AUIPC needs the PC on this input.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Make one local operand-routing optimization: give AUIPC a dedicated
PC-relative result arm and feed ordinary ALU operand A directly from
the existing fully forwarded rs1. Keep the same pipeline registers,
instruction latencies, forwarding priority and issue schedule.

Add ALU_AUIPC = 5'd19 without renumbering any existing operation.
Inside the decoder's validated AUIPC opcode arm, select ALU_AUIPC
while retaining is_auipc, alu_src, reg_write and default-illegal
discipline. In EX, wire alu_a directly to post-forwarding rs1.
Reuse the existing full-width branch_target = in.pc + in.imm sum as
a new internal ALU input named pc_relative_result. The ALU case arm
for ALU_AUIPC returns this input directly. This is the modulo-2^32
AUIPC result, with no AUIPC operand mux before the generic ALU and
no register/immediate mux before its dedicated PC-relative addition.
Place AUIPC selection within the existing ALU result case, rather
than adding a new external mux after that case or another EX/MEM bank.

Every ordinary ALU operation must continue using a = forwarded rs1
and the existing immediate-or-forwarded-rs2 b. AUIPC alone selects
pc_relative_result. Keep the champion's explicit five-level shared
SRL/SRA network, independent SLL, all other ALU results and all eight
exact ALTOPS expressions. Preserve the dedicated LSU address sum,
MEM multiplier, blocking divider and divider metadata. RVFI source
values remain architectural forwarded operands, including AUIPC's
existing source-field convention. Preserve alignment traps, decoder
legality, x0, bus handshakes, all hold/flush priorities, retained WB
forwarding, nret=1 ports and exactly-once ordered retirement.

title: Select narrow branch relation flags after comparing bypass candidates
motivation:
The champion scores 199.86 iter/sec at 90.490 MHz and 4,527,646
marker-bounded cycles. LESSONS.md is absent. Structural r9s1 added
dependency latency and lost fitness despite 103.173 MHz; r10s1 added
result banks and forwarding fanout and fell to 77.992 MHz. The recorded
champion critical path traverses forwarded operands, EX branch recovery
and ID control. This proposal isolates that control path without adding
stages, changing the ALU or changing instruction latency.

hypothesis.motivation:
The champion scores 199.86 iter/sec at 90.490 MHz and 4,527,646
marker-bounded cycles. LESSONS.md is absent. Structural r9s1 added
dependency latency and lost fitness despite 103.173 MHz; r10s1 added

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace the branch comparator after the two 32-bit forwarding muxes with
a small relation matrix over the existing registered operand candidates.
Evaluate equality, unsigned-less and signed-less before choosing the
forwarding sources, select only these three relation bits, and decode
branch_op once afterward. This is one structural relocation of branch
operand arbitration across comparison. Keep the ordinary ALU, shifter,
address generation, divider and all architectural operand muxes unchanged.

Let A[0]=in.rs1_val, A[1]=fwd_ex_mem, A[2]=fwd_mem_wb;
let B[0]=in.rs2_val, B[1]=fwd_ex_mem, B[2]=fwd_mem_wb.
The existing qualified fwd_rs1_sel and fwd_rs2_sel choose one candidate
each. For a source selector, derive three local one-hot enables for saved,
early and WB sources, preserving the existing default-to-saved behavior.
Do not introduce additional producer sources, bank kinds or qualification
into forward_unit. Candidate evaluation has no side effects.

For each distinct candidate pair compute eq=(A==B) and ltu=(A<B).
Compute signed-less by sharing the unsigned comparison:
lts=(A[31] ^ B[31]) ? A[31] : ltu.
Represent each pair's flags as {lts,ltu,eq}. Avoid a separate signed
subtract/compare tree. Only six independent pairs are needed:
(A0,B0), (A0,early), (A0,WB), (early,B0), (WB,B0), and (early,WB).
The early/early and WB/WB diagonal pairs are always {0,0,1}.
Derive the reversed WB/early pair from early/WB flags:
eq_rev=eq; ltu_rev=!ltu && !eq; lts_rev=!lts && !eq.
These identities apply to both signed and unsigned total ordering.
Preserve all 32 operand bits; do not truncate comparisons or assume
sign bits agree because register numbers or destination matches agree.

Select the three-bit relation result with a balanced masked-OR tree,
first across the three rs2 candidates and then across the three rs1
candidates. Branch operation decode appears only AFTER flag selection:
BEQ=eq, BNE=!eq, BLT=lts, BGE=!lts, BLTU=ltu, BGEU=!ltu;
reserved branch operations produce false as today. Do not distribute
branch_op decoding to each candidate comparator. Do not replace this
with nine copies of a complete operation-dependent predicate or ALU.
The selected relation is exactly the relation of the same architectural
rs1/rs2 that the existing forwarding muxes choose.

Use this result for the existing branch_cond, then preserve the current
branch_taken, valid qualification, target calculation, alignment checks,
redirect-over-stall priority and ID squash controls. Keep EX branch
resolution in its current cycle; no predictor, early decode redirect,
registered delayed recovery or extra branch bubble is added. Unselected
candidate relations cannot cause a trap or redirect. JAL/JALR behavior,
link values, target addresses and fault suppression remain unchanged.

Retain the original selected full-width rs1 and rs2 for the ALU, store
data, LSU/JALR address calculation, real divider requests, EX/MEM source
snapshots, MEM multiplier operands and RVFI. Preserve ID-aligned raw
forwarding-match capture, EX/MEM-over-WB priority, x0 treatment, current
producer write eligibility and retained MEM/WB forwarding during stalls.
Branch comparisons must remain correct when a source comes from a held
WB producer whose retirement valid was cleared; use the authoritative
existing selectors rather than adding new valid gates. Use the same
relation topology in real and RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS builds, preserving
every exact M-extension substitute and real arithmetic unit.

Private probes in this research turn provide negative evidence for
broader versions: nine complete ALU lanes reached only 66.049 MHz;
a transparent fetch buffer saved 3.668 percent cycles and passed all
53 unchanged formal checks but reached only 85.553 MHz median; nine
complete operation-dependent branch predicates reached 79.730 MHz.
None is proposed or evidence of a fitness improvement. The final
relation-only version specifically removes replicated branch-op
selection, shares signed/unsigned comparison, uses constant diagonals
and shares the reversed producer pair to reduce replication and fanout.
Its timing and correctness results must be recorded before treating
the forecast as measured; an ongoing private probe is only preliminary.

Forecast an unmeasured eight percent fitness gain with low confidence.
At the unchanged champion cycle count, acceptance above 209.05356
iter/sec requires median Gowin Fmax above approximately 94.653 MHz.
The intended benefit is removing forwarding selection from the inputs
of branch reduction/carry chains while selecting only three bits after
comparison. The competing shift path, flag selection latency, additional
operand fanout and placement are the main risks; the unsuccessful broader
predicate matrix makes this a deliberately low-confidence hypothesis.
Require three-option vendor timing, unchanged formal gates, retirement
cosim and canonical marker-bounded CoreMark validation. Preserve nret=1,
all ports and all hard invariants; change no evaluator file or check.
