title: Small agree predictor learns exceptions to static branch bias
motivation:
The champion scores 199.86 iter/sec at 90.490 MHz with 4527646
marker-bounded cycles. LESSONS.md is absent. Prior predictor entries
in experiments/log.jsonl were reviewed: r8s2's sixteen-entry bimodal
direction predictor used 4254282 cycles but fell to 83.849 MHz;
r9s2's stateless opcode-biased prediction used 4253728 cycles and
reached 87.379 MHz, scoring 205.42 and missing the 209.05356 acceptance
threshold. Cached-target predictors also lost clock speed. A small
predictor should learn deviations from the successful static policy,
while reducing destructive aliasing between oppositely biased branches
and avoiding target storage, tag checks and wide prediction metadata.

hypothesis.motivation:
The champion scores 199.86 iter/sec at 90.490 MHz with 4527646
marker-bounded cycles. LESSONS.md is absent. Prior predictor entries
in experiments/log.jsonl were reviewed: r8s2's sixteen-entry bimodal
direction predictor used 4254282 cycles but fell to 83.849 MHz;
r9s2's stateless opcode-biased prediction used 4253728 cycles and
reached 87.379 MHz, scoring 205.42 and missing the 209.05356 acceptance
threshold. Cached-target predictors also lost clock speed. A small
predictor should learn deviations from the successful static policy,
while reducing destructive aliasing between oppositely biased branches
and avoiding target storage, tag checks and wide prediction metadata.
hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add one 16-entry agree direction predictor to the current champion.
Every entry is a two-bit saturating counter representing agreement
with an instruction-derived static bias, rather than raw taken
direction. Index with fetch PC[5:2] XOR PC[10:7], a four-bit folded PC index. For legal conditional branches,
bias = instr[14] ? instr[31] : instr[12]: BEQ is biased not taken,
BNE taken, and signed/unsigned inequalities backward taken and forward
not taken. Reset counters to strongly agree (2'b11). Predict the
bias when counter[1] is one and its complement otherwise. Train up
for agreement between actual direction and the captured bias, down
for disagreement, saturating at 0 and 3. Aliased branches with opposite
directions but matching their own biases reinforce the same state.
This is a single small direction-prediction experiment; there is no
target table, tag, return stack, global history or pipeline-depth change.

Consult counters only for positively validated BRANCH encodings;
reserved funct3 values predict fall-through. Predict legal aligned
JAL taken directly from its actual instruction. Leave JALR unpredicted.
Generate every direct target from the current raw imem instruction
and its complete original PC. Use exact split-carry B/J additions:
for B compute the low twelve-bit sum with carry and parallel upper
twenty-bit PC+1/PC-1 candidates; carry equal to offset sign selects
unchanged high bits, positive carry selects increment, and negative
no-carry selects decrement. Use the corresponding low twenty/high
twelve construction for JAL. These are exact modulo-2^32 sums,
including boundary crossings and wraparound. Verify their equivalence
to full-width addition. Qualify taken prediction with word alignment.

Implement counters as independent constant-index registers with local
update enables and a balanced lookup of just their agreement MSBs.
Do not introduce a wide target lookup or a combinational EX-to-counter
write path. Carry only the actually selected predicted_taken bit
through if_id_t and id_ex_t. Its payload capture/hold conditions match
the original PC/instruction; keep recovery out of raw imem data,
source addresses and wide ID payload data and enables. The static bias
used for training is recomputed from the held EX instruction, whose
bits are exactly those used for the original prediction.

Reuse the prior narrow recovery strategy. Resolve architectural
branch predicates from fully forwarded operands using parallel
eight-bit equality/less-than lanes and a balanced significance merge.
Share these exact predicates between architectural branch direction
and misprediction detection. Move branch inversion into the early
register-only polarity branch_op[0] XOR predicted_taken so recovery
does not serialize two late XOR operations. Keep all six branch
comparisons equivalent to RV32I. For a legal aligned conditional
branch, recovery is actual direction XOR carried predicted_taken.
A correctly predicted JAL causes no recovery. Aligned JALR retains
its existing forwarded-target recovery path. Faulting direct targets
predict fall-through, retaining existing traps and suppressed links.

Flatten the predictor's PC successor selection into mutually exclusive
masked terms combined by a balanced OR: hold PC, accepted PC+4,
accepted predicted B target, accepted predicted J target, or repair
target. Repair masks all ordinary terms; stalls select hold unless
an accepted repair overrides them. Register this complete next-PC
each clock with reset priority. Avoid a serial B/J mux followed by
taken/fall-through, repair, and late PC clock-enable selection. This
is the timing-sensitive integration of this direction predictor, with
unchanged acceptance and recovery semantics.

Preselect a conditional repair target from the carried prediction:
original PC+4 for an incorrect taken prediction, original PC+imm
for an incorrect fall-through prediction. The late branch comparator
controls only the recovery event, not a second wide target mux.
Architectural pc_next and RVFI always use the true resolved outcome.
Assert that accepted recovery targets equal architectural successors
and that any selected prediction belongs to a legal aligned direct
transfer. Because targets come from the same fetched PC/instruction,
counter aliases or arbitrary counter state can change performance
but cannot redirect a direct instruction to a wrong destination.

Predicted PC advancement must coincide with valid ID/EX acceptance.
Imem backpressure, load/multiply-use bubbles, older dmem freezes and
unfinished division do not consume predictions. Hold prediction
metadata with its live instruction. Gate recovery by valid actual
EX advancement, excluding dmem freezes and unfinished division;
accepted recovery overrides imem and load-use holds. Correct
predictions admit a ready target instruction without a squash.

Register training at the EX/MEM boundary in a separate compact record
containing a four-bit folded index, one agreement bit and one valid bit.
Capture only legal aligned conditional branches when EX advances;
hold the record with EX/MEM during dmem freezes and emit invalid
records for bubbles and divider waits. Consume each record once on
MEM advancement. Forwarded comparisons therefore drive local update
flops instead of all predictor write enables in the same cycle.
A valid counter write uses the captured agreement, not current fetch
bits or a held/repeated branch. No predictor state or training target
is added to divider metadata. Jumps, traps and bubbles never train.

Forecast a seven percent fitness improvement with low confidence.
The intended gain is better conditional accuracy and fewer harmful
direction aliases with a small state and recovery footprint. Protecting
median Fmax is essential: prior predictors demonstrate that cycle
reduction alone is insufficient. Measure actual marker-bounded
CoreMark cycles and all three vendor placement options; require a
score greater than 209.05356 iter/sec. This forecast is unmeasured.
Preserve the champion's arithmetic, effective-address lane, MEM
multiplier, unified WB result, registered forwarding matches,
load/multiply interlock, retained MEM/WB forwarding and divider
handshakes. Keep nret=1, all top-level IO, exact RVFI retirement/order,
decoder legality, alignment traps and every invariant and evaluator
file unchanged.

title: Retimed late completion for shifts and prediction-error recovery
motivation:
The champion scores 212.70 iter/sec at median Gowin Fmax 89.967 MHz
and 4,229,842 marked CoreMark cycles. LESSONS.md is absent; all prior
structural log entries were reviewed. The early-ALU/late-multiply
topology succeeded in r6s1. Delaying every taken transfer in r2s1,
adding general dependency stages in r9s1, and replicating result banks
or relations in r10s1/r11s1 failed. The new agree predictor makes later
recovery cheaper: correctly predicted transfers need no squash.
Private recovery-only probes exposed the competing forwarded shifter
path and missed acceptance, as did earlier forwarding arbitration.
A coordinated completion boundary must cut both competing EX paths
while retaining immediate forwarding for ordinary ALU operations.

the existing EX/MEM boundary. Keep ordinary integer results available
in EX/MEM, but complete all barrel shifts from captured operands in

event. This is one structural retiming of execution completion. Keep
the existing stage count, single issue, retirement boundary and nret=1;

into EX/MEM rs1_val and rs2_val. No bundle extension is needed.

in.ctrl.alu_src ? in.instr[24:20] : in.rs2_val[4:0].

is_shift ? shift_result : in.alu_result.

unchanged; no combinational MEM-to-EX shift bypass is permitted.

Exclude all three shift operation codes from EX/MEM's registered

to the existing late-producer hazard input alongside load and multiply.

obtains the result from registered WB. Independent instructions and
independent shifts still issue each clock. Preserve current forwarding
selectors, registered raw dependency matches, youngest-writer priority,
write-first register reads and retained MEM/WB forwarding during holds.

title: Register agree-predictor recovery to break the EX-to-fetch path
motivation:
LESSONS.md is absent. The predictor history was reviewed: cached-target
attempts r1s2 through r7s2 repeatedly sacrificed clock speed, while
r11s2's small agree predictor improved fitness to 212.70 iter/sec at
89.967 MHz and 4,229,842 marked CoreMark cycles. Its reported worst
path starts at a registered forwarding match and reaches the fetch PC
through EX and ID. Prediction accuracy has made recovery less frequent,
but the forwarded branch comparison and immediate recovery still set
the clock period for every instruction. Registering this infrequent
event can trade one extra cycle per mistake for a faster common case.

Apply the same registered recovery boundary to unpredicted JALR, so
its forwarded target adder cannot retain an EX-to-fetch bypass around
the new boundary. Correctly predicted branches and JAL still admit
the ready target fetch without any bubble. Conditional mistakes and
JALR pay two recovery bubbles instead of one; no extra normal pipeline
stage, target table, history bank or direction-policy change is added.

The EX event retains all six RV32I predicates and existing alignment
and illegal-instruction rules. Capture it only when a valid EX
instruction actually advances, with neither an older dmem freeze nor
an unfinished divider operation. Capture the repair destination from
the existing authoritative architectural successor; preserve exact
original-PC targets, fall-through, JALR bit-zero clearing, links and
traps. Keep repair state separate from div_metadata_q. A dmem hold
retains the pending record; bubbles and divider waits emit no event.
Valid recovery is consumed once when its owning MEM instruction
advances. A previously consumed record must never redirect again.

On a registered MEM recovery, the owning older instruction advances
to WB normally and retires once. Repair fetch PC to its registered
successor, invalidate the current fetched instruction, clear ID/EX
controls, and force the younger EX/MEM result to a side-effect-free

The younger EX instruction must neither enter MEM nor write a register,

Wide ID payload still uses ordinary reset/hold capture; recovery

Registered older recovery takes priority over younger load/multiply

Explicitly suppress divider request acceptance and completion transfer
for a squashed younger EX instruction, clear its execute-hold influence

Since the repairing control instruction could not advance to MEM
while an older EX/MEM memory request was stalled, its normal recovery

backpressure and the existing retained MEM/WB forwarding data.
No wrong-path memory operation may acquire EX/MEM memory controls.

Keep agree-counter updates at their current MEM advancement boundary.
The repairing branch's already registered training record is valid
and should be consumed exactly once; suppress only the younger EX

motivation:

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace only the combinational ADD/SUB implementation in alu.sv
with one shared 32-bit adder using four eight-bit blocks, parallel
local carry-in candidates and explicit block carry lookahead. Keep
the ALU ports, EX/MEM result boundary and all instruction latencies.
This is one carry-network optimization, with no pipeline retiming,
predictor change, register-file rewrite or extra execution cycle.

Let subtract = (op == ALU_SUB), Bx = b ^ {32{subtract}}, and
C0 = subtract. For each eight-bit block i, compute nine-bit local
candidate sums S0[i] = {1'b0,Ai} + {1'b0,Bxi} and
S1[i] = {1'b0,Ai} + {1'b0,Bxi} + 9'd1 in parallel, directly from

C1 = G0 | (P0 & C0);
C2 = G1 | (P1 & G0) | (P1 & P0 & C0);

title: Carry-select arithmetic across the EX/MEM boundary without dependency bubbles
motivation:
The champion scores 224.09 iter/sec at 98.964 MHz and 4,416,239 marked
cycles. Its worst Gowin path starts at registered WB data and ends at
EX/MEM alu_result through forwarding and the ordinary ALU: 15.766 ns,
23 cells. LESSONS.md is absent. The structural history shows that adding
a general operand stage in r9s1 reached 103.173 MHz but lost fitness
because dependent instructions needed extra bubbles. r10s1's separate
operation banks and expanded bypass arbitration also regressed. The
successful r6s1 and r12s1 changes instead used the existing EX/MEM
boundary to remove arithmetic depth. Retiming carry selection, rather
than delaying instruction availability, targets the remaining path.

cycles. Its worst Gowin path starts at registered WB data and ends at

23 cells. LESSONS.md is absent. The structural history shows that adding
a general operand stage in r9s1 reached 103.173 MHz but lost fitness
because dependent instructions needed extra bubbles. r10s1's separate

boundary to remove arithmetic depth. Retiming carry selection, rather
than delaying instruction availability, targets the remaining path.
hypothesis.hypothesis:
Change the EX/MEM representation of ADD/SUB results from a completed
32-bit word to registered byte-sized carry-select fragments. Compute
independent eight-bit sums in EX, then assemble the full architectural
word from those registered fragments on the MEM side of the same
boundary. This is one structural retiming of integer arithmetic.
Preserve the instruction stages, one-instruction issue rate, nret=1,
retirement boundary, and immediate ADD/SUB forwarding availability.

For legal ALU_ADD and ALU_SUB instructions other than jump links, use
the existing fully forwarded and selected alu_a and alu_b. Let sub be
the exact ALU_SUB match, B = alu_b XOR {32{sub}}, and carry_in = sub.
Compute the low byte as a nine-bit sum of A[7:0], B[7:0], and carry_in.
For bytes 1, 2, and 3 independently compute nine-bit candidate sums
S0[k] = {0,A_byte} + {0,B_byte} and S1[k] = S0[k] + 9'd1.
Register the low-byte result/carry, each upper byte's two candidate
results, and its carry summary. There must be no carry dependency
between bytes before this register. Preserve all 32 architectural
operand bits and modulo-2^32 wraparound. AUIPC uses its current PC
operand and follows this same ADD representation.

After EX/MEM, define G[k] = registered S0[k][8] and
P[k] = registered S1[k][8]. Then C1 is the registered low-byte carry,
C2 = G1 OR (P1 AND C1), and
C3 = G2 OR (P2 AND G1) OR (P2 AND P1 AND C1).
Choose each upper result byte between its registered S0 and S1 with
the corresponding carry. Compute these boundary carries in parallel
with the explicit lookahead equations, not a serial chain of byte
additions or a new 32-bit adder after the register. The top carry is
discarded. Keep non-arithmetic results on the existing registered
ordinary-result word and use a registered arithmetic-kind bit to
select the reconstructed arithmetic word on the EX/MEM output.

Implement the fragments as private EX/MEM-aligned state inside
ex_stage or a dedicated module. The public ex_mem_t.alu_result remains
the exact completed 32-bit architectural result, so MEM selection and
the existing three-source forwarding interface need no new bank or
producer tag. The fragment state resets deterministically and holds
on exactly the existing downstream stall. Qualify arithmetic-kind
with valid legal ADD/SUB and the existing non-jump result selection;
divider waiting/completion and older recovery squash clear its
eligibility. Keep squash out of wide fragment data D muxes and hold
enables; irrelevant fragments may capture during bubbles. Divider
completion always chooses its existing captured registered result.

Add a default-enabled ALU parameter allowing only the EX instance to
omit ordinary ALU_ADD/ALU_SUB hardware, since EX now builds those
results with the fragment lane. The standalone ALU retains its exact
interface and results. Preserve SLT/SLTU, Boolean operations, LUI,
all shift handling, every exact RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS formula, and real
M-extension arithmetic. In particular, ALTOPS M operations that use
addition/subtraction must retain their original expressions; the
parameter affects only the two base-operation case arms. Do not
reroute LSU effective-address or JALR target arithmetic through the
partial result, or change registered recovery and predictor training.

Feed the reconstructed word into both current EX/MEM forwarding and
normal MEM/WB ordinary-result selection. ADD/SUB stays fwd_ready in
its original cycle; insert no new arithmetic interlock and add no
combinational MEM/WB completion selector. WB still exposes only the
unified registered wb_result. Retain youngest-writer priority, raw
registered dependency matches, write-first regfile reads, x0, and the
special retained WB forwarding value across memory stalls. A chain
of dependent ADD/SUB instructions must keep its current schedule.

Keep legal/illegal decoding, all alignment traps, bus handshakes,
captured architectural RVFI sources and results, contiguous channel-0
retirement orders, and every evaluation check unchanged. Directed
tests must cover carry/borrow propagation across every byte boundary,
all-ones and signed extrema, AUIPC, every forwarding-source pairing,
dependent arithmetic/store/branch/JALR consumers, long memory holds,
divider transfers, bubbles and wrong-path squashes. Compare completed
fragment words with exact 32-bit addition/subtraction and check no
arithmetic dependency bubble was introduced.

Forecast a ten percent fitness increase with low confidence, entirely
from Fmax at unchanged marked cycles. No prototype result is claimed.
The principal risk is the reconstructed early-forwarding path becoming
critical, followed by the unchanged LSU adder, SLT or MEM completion.
The replicated upper-byte candidates also add registers and routing.
Evaluate the actual median of all three Gowin placement options and
the canonical marker-bounded CoreMark run. Acceptance requires fitness
above 234.39814 iter/sec, approximately 103.52 MHz if cycles remain
4,416,239. Preserve the canonical CRC/UART/bounds/marker validation,
unchanged formal configuration and full retirement-reference cosim.

title: Finish agree-prediction validation from registered branch relations
motivation:
LESSONS.md is absent. The predictor history was reviewed: cached-target
predictors repeatedly lost clock speed, whereas r11s2's small agree
predictor improved fitness. The current r12s1 champion already applies
recovery from EX/MEM and scores 224.09 iter/sec at 98.964 MHz with
4416239 marked cycles. Merely registering recovery again is redundant.
The remaining EX branch comparison still consumes forwarded operands,
completes its full significance merge and produces trap, recovery and
training decisions before the register. Prediction validation can be
split at that existing register without adding a recovery cycle.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Retain the existing sixteen-counter agree prediction policy and direct
B/J fetch targets. Change only the implementation of conditional
prediction validation: register the four eight-bit equality and ordered
less-than relations at EX/MEM, then finish their balanced significance
merge and prediction mismatch in MEM. Keep the comparator's exact
signed/unsigned top-byte transformation. EX ends at eight relation
bits; no completed conditional direction, mismatch, or conditional
target-fault predicate may continue to feed timed EX register controls.

Capture the original branch operation/polarity, predicted_taken, folded
index, instruction-derived bias, branch-target alignment and legal
conditional eligibility alongside those relations. Hold this compact
record with EX/MEM. Its event validity requires actual EX advancement,
an instruction valid and legal in the decoder, no unfinished division,
and no older recovery squash. Bubbles and squashed younger branches
cannot generate prediction validation or training events. Keep this
record separate from div_metadata_q and ordinary arithmetic payloads.

In MEM derive branch_base from the registered lane relations, actual
condition = branch_base XOR branch_op[0], and mismatch = branch_base
XOR (branch_op[0] XOR predicted_taken). Use the register-only polarity
early, retaining the existing narrow recovery formulation. The existing
EX/MEM recovery-target register continues to capture the destination
preselected solely by predicted_taken: original PC+4 for a predicted
taken branch and original PC+imm otherwise. An aligned legal branch
redirects iff the MEM comparison detects a mismatch. Keep JAL/JALR
recovery eligibility and authoritative target captured in EX as today;
there is no new target table, prediction scheme or EX-to-fetch bypass.

This preserves the champion's recovery schedule: branch in EX produces
relation flops on an edge, and its MEM cycle applies repair on the next
edge, exactly when recovery_valid_q currently repairs fetch. Correct
predictions still allow the ready target instruction to advance.
Accepted MEM repair squashes both younger positions through the existing
ID flush and EX control-only squash, including wrong-path divider
launch suppression. Genuine dmem holds retain the record, while repair
consumption and training remain qualified by MEM advancement. Recovery
retains priority over younger dependencies and imem unavailability.

Move conditional architectural successor and conditional target-trap
completion to MEM as well, so an ostensibly verification-only full
comparator is not left feeding timed EX ctrl/fwd_ready registers.
A branch has no register-write or memory side effect before this
boundary. Preserve the decoder's default-illegal control unchanged in
EX; in MEM add the conditional target fault only when the legal branch
actually takes a misaligned target. That fault reports trap and PC+4.
Otherwise MEM/WB captures PC+imm for taken and PC+4 for not taken.
Jumps retain their exact EX alignment, suppressed-link and successor
handling. MEM load/store alignment and arithmetic completion stay as
they are. RVFI always reports the resolved architectural successor.

Generate the existing index/agreement/valid training interface from the
same registered relations during MEM. Agreement compares the actual
condition with the captured static bias. The predictor consumes it on
that MEM advancement edge, preserving the current learning latency and
exactly-once counter updates. Do not add a further training register or
train from the younger EX instruction on a recovery edge. Prediction
state changes only for legal aligned conditional branches.

The timing hypothesis is that cutting the EX branch significance merge
and conditional trap/control fanout reduces competition with the
forwarded ALU lane, while MEM recovery starts from small local relation
flops rather than a 32-bit forwarded comparator. Keep independent
relation registers and a balanced merge; avoid copying a full operand
comparator into MEM or retaining its completed EX counterpart. The
main risk is that the short MEM merge plus recovery-to-squash path
becomes critical, or that placement changes do not help the current
WB-to-EX ALU path. Forecast seven percent fitness gain with low
confidence; this is an unmeasured timing hypothesis, not an IPC claim.
With unchanged marked cycles, acceptance above 234.39814 iter/sec
requires median Gowin Fmax above approximately 103.52 MHz. Measure all
three placement options and actual marker-bounded cycles; preserve
nret=1, external IO, all arithmetic, exact RVFI order/operands, decoder
legality, traps, memory bounds, canonical CRC/UART and every eval gate.

title: Early completion for one-bit and two-bit immediate shifts
motivation: The r12s1 champion scores 224.09 iter/sec at 98.964 MHz and 4,416,239 marked cycles. It moved every shift to MEM to remove the five-level barrel shifter from the forwarded EX path, at the cost of shift-use bubbles. Immediate shifts by one or two bits need only fixed wiring and a single count-selection level. Returning just those operations to early completion can recover cycles while keeping general shifts off EX. LESSONS.md is absent. The micro_opt history, including r8s0's shared right shifter, r11s0's operand rewrite and r13s0's failed carry-lookahead change, was reviewed. Isolated local timing prototypes in this turn also failed to beat the champion, so a further clock-only mux or carry rewrite is less promising than this narrow shift fast path.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add one local fixed-count completion path for legal SLLI, SRLI and SRAI whose encoded shamt is exactly 1 or 2. Keep the pipeline topology, retirement boundary and general late-shift implementation. This is one micro optimization to the existing shift execution policy, rather than restoring a variable barrel shifter or adding a stage.

Define fast_shift in EX from in.valid, !in.ctrl.is_illegal, in.ctrl.alu_src, an ALU_SLL/SRL/SRA operation, and in.instr[24:20] equal to 5'd1 or 5'd2. Derive the same classification from ID/EX in core.sv for the existing shift-use interlock. All register shifts, all other immediate counts, and invalid or illegal instructions retain their existing behavior. In particular, a register shift whose runtime count happens to equal 1 or 2 remains late.

Extend alu.sv with a default-disabled fixed-shift parameter for the EX instance only. When ENABLE_SHIFTS is false and the fixed path is enabled, construct left results from {a[30:0],1'b0} and {a[29:0],2'b00}; construct right results from {fill,a[31:1]} and {{2{fill}},a[31:2]}, with fill = (op == ALU_SRA) && a[31]. Select between counts 1 and 2 using the registered immediate count, through at most one data selection level. Use the existing shift arms of the ALU result case, rather than appending a new mux after the completed ordinary ALU result. The selected ALU a and b remain fully forwarded and retain the existing AUIPC/immediate routing. For fast shifts, b is the decoded immediate, so its low five bits are the exact validated count. The partial EX shift result for any non-fast shift is deliberately provisional and must never become an architectural or early-forwarded result.

Capture a fast_shift bit in EX/MEM alongside the owning instruction. Include it in normal payload and divider metadata initialization, reset it deterministically, retain it on exactly the existing dmem hold and clear its eligibility on an older recovery squash. Set fwd_ready for eligible fast shifts in their normal EX completion cycle. Keep MUL and every non-fast shift ineligible for EX/MEM forwarding. Exclude only fast shifts from id_ex_shift's late-result hazard predicate; genuine load, multiply and other shift dependencies retain their existing single-cycle interlock. Do not mask raw source comparisons or change youngest-writer forwarding priority.

In MEM, qualify the late-shift result selector with !in.fast_shift. A fast shift uses its captured in.alu_result through the existing ordinary-result arm, while every other shift still uses the original five-level MEM network. Preserve the unified registered wb_result, held WB forwarding after valid clears, exact architectural source values and result selection under both bus stalls. This is essential: without the MEM selection change, early forwarding could differ from retirement. Preserve ALTOPS formulas and standalone ALU full-shift behavior; this fast-path parameter must not alter default arithmetic tests or any M-extension operation.

Forecast an unmeasured six percent fitness gain with low confidence. The intended benefit is fewer one-bit/two-bit immediate shift-use bubbles with a much shallower EX shift network than the general barrel shifter. Extra ALU result selection and fast eligibility fanout can reduce Fmax, and the actual frequency of these dependencies can limit cycle savings. No successful prototype or measured speedup is claimed for this final candidate. Measure marker-bounded cycles and the median of all three Gowin placement options; acceptance requires fitness strictly above 234.39814 iter/sec. Preserve the existing nret=1 IO and contiguous retirement order, decoder default-illegal discipline, all alignment traps, predictor/recovery timing, memory handshakes and bounds, canonical CRC/UART validation and every evaluator check.

title: Decouple fetch with a two-entry elastic instruction queue
motivation:
The champion scores 224.09 iter/sec at 98.964 MHz and 4,416,239 marked
CoreMark cycles. Instruction and data buses each inject about 22 percent
stalls, but fetch currently stops on every data-memory hold, divider wait
and late-result dependency. The combinational IF/ID connection cannot
save an instruction delivered during these holds. LESSONS.md is absent.
Structural history shows that an extra operand stage lost fitness through
dependency bubbles (r9s1), while result banks and carry fragments also
regressed (r10s1/r13s1). An r11s1 private one-entry transparent fetch-buffer
probe saved 3.668 percent cycles but reached only 85.553 MHz on the older
immediate-recovery topology. This proposal tests deeper fetch elasticity
on the current registered-recovery core without delaying ALU results.

Structural history shows that an extra operand stage lost fitness through
dependency bubbles (r9s1), while result banks and carry fragments also
regressed (r10s1/r13s1). An r11s1 private one-entry transparent fetch-buffer
probe saved 3.668 percent cycles but reached only 85.553 MHz on the older
immediate-recovery topology. This proposal tests deeper fetch elasticity
on the current registered-recovery core without delaying ALU results.

Insert a two-entry, flop-based elastic instruction queue between fetch
and the existing decode/ID-EX boundary. Give fetch its own admission
enable rather than stopping it whenever the consumer is held. Preserve
single issue, the existing execution/MEM/WB stages, all arithmetic and
forwarding latencies, the agree predictor, registered recovery and nret=1.
This is one structural change to producer-consumer coupling.

Each entry contains the exact fetched PC, instruction and predicted_taken
bit. Declare two separate if_id_t flop registers, entry0_q and entry1_q,
with two-bit count_q and one-bit read_q/write_q. Use no RAM or shifting
payload array. In particular avoid unpacked arrays of packed structs:
a private probe exposed incorrect Yosys formal elaboration of that
representation, resolved by separate named entry registers.

When empty, bypass a ready response directly to ID in the current cycle.
If ID cannot accept it, enqueue it instead. With queued data, ID sees
the oldest entry independently of CURRENT io_imemReady. Define
head_ready = (count_q != 0) || io_imemReady and
capacity = (count_q != 2).
Capacity depends ONLY on registered occupancy, never same-cycle dequeue.
A full queue may dequeue but cannot refill until the following cycle.
Simultaneous push/pop is supported at occupancy one. This deliberate
full-queue turnaround removes head/hazard feedback from fetch-PC control.

Retain the existing if_stage.sv and hazard_unit.sv RTL. In core.sv wire
IF.stall to !capacity || !io_imemReady, IF.flush to
redirect || !io_imemReady, and IF.out to the queue's raw response.
Select raw when count_q is zero, otherwise read_q ? entry1_q : entry0_q;
override only head.valid with head_ready && !redirect. Feed this selected
bundle to ID, its raw source fields to the existing hazard comparisons,
and head_ready to hazard_unit.imem_ready. Existing stall_id/flush_id and
downstream controls retain their meaning. The original combined
stall_if/flush_if outputs no longer control IF; they may remain unused.

For concrete queue control let take = !stall_id && !flush_id,
pop = (count_q != 0) && take && !redirect,
bypass = (count_q == 0) && take, and
push = io_imemReady && capacity && !bypass && !redirect.
Increment/decrement count_q on push-only/pop-only; hold it when both or
neither occur. Toggle read_q on pop and write_q on push. Reset or accepted
redirect clears count_q and both pointers. A ready response becomes
exactly one live token, either directly captured by ID or queued.

Separate payload capture from those live-token controls. Enable entry0_q
capture on io_imemReady && capacity && !write_q and entry1_q on
io_imemReady && capacity && write_q, each capturing the raw IF bundle.
Do NOT use push, take, pop, reset or redirect in these wide entry data
muxes or enables. Empty bypass and reset/recovery may capture irrelevant
payload without creating a queued token. Occupancy and pointers alone
decide which captured word is live. This exact separation prevents the
head/hazard-to-wide-write-enable timing path. Each entry uses its own
constant destination and local write enable, with no dynamic array write.

The existing IF PC remains the memory request address and advances
exactly when a ready response has capacity and no older redirect.
Retain its existing agree lookup, bias, direct B/J target arithmetic,
modulo-32-bit targets and alignment/legality qualifications. Apply
prediction to the raw fetched instruction and fetch PC, then store the
predicted_taken bit with its owning instruction. Do not predict again
from queued data or use the dequeue PC for fetch lookup. Correct direct
predictions preserve the queued target stream even if predictor counters
change before dequeue. No new prediction scheme or target table is added.

A missing head injects the existing ID control bubble while older stages
advance. Late load/multiply/shift-use injects the existing dependency
bubble without consuming its waiting head. Dmem/divider holds also retain
that head, while fetch may continue admitting responses until full.

dependency matches, youngest-writer priority, x0, write-first regfile
reads and retained WB forwarding data. Queueing instructions is not an
operand stage; independent and immediately dependent ordinary ALU
instructions retain their current execution and forwarding schedules.

Accepted older EX/MEM recovery overrides all queue admissions, dequeues,
prediction successors and younger dependencies. Clear compact queue
state and redirect the request PC on that edge; discard the old response
even when ready. Retain existing ID flush and control-only younger EX
squash, divider request/result/hold suppression and exactly-once training.
Keep recovery out of queue payload muxes/enables; invalidating occupancy

memory, write registers, launch division, train prediction or retire.
Preserve stable downstream memory requests, divider snapshots/completion,
all alignment traps, decoder default illegal, exact RVFI operands and
architectural successors, contiguous channel-0 order and declared nret=1

motivation:
LESSONS.md is absent. Predictor history was reviewed: the small agree
predictor succeeded, while target tables and recovery retiming regressed.
The champion scores 224.09 iter/sec at 98.964 MHz and 4416239 marked
cycles. Conditional branch resolution currently reaches not only prediction
repair/training but also EX trap, reg_write and fwd_ready through taken-
target misalignment. A conditional branch has no register or memory result,
so that target-fault control fanout is unnecessary for timed execution.
Isolate it from result eligibility without changing prediction or repair.

metadata, but must not reach timed EX result eligibility via a branch
alignment fault. Remove misalign_branch from the EX ctrl_with_trap

including illegal reporting and link suppression, exactly as today.

This is safe because positively decoded conditional branches already have
reg_write=0, mem_read=0 and mem_write=0, with ALU_ADD and no DIV request.
Their taken-target fault cannot suppress an architectural result that
exists. Preserve the decoder's original is_illegal value, all controls
on illegal encodings, and the existing raw branch_taken/branch_target
EX/MEM fields. Preserve full exact comparison, signed/unsigned handling
and prediction mismatch in EX; do not move comparisons into MEM or
introduce another recovery cycle. The current alignment gate on recovery
and training remains unchanged, so a misaligned branch target neither
redirects nor trains. IF already predicts only aligned direct targets.

At the existing MEM/WB capture, add the conditional branch fault to the
retiring is_illegal bit: owning EX/MEM ctrl.is_branch AND captured
branch_taken AND branch_target[1:0]!=0. Keep this completion strictly on
the retirement trap path. It must not feed MEM multiplier/shift enables,
load/store requests, reg_write, forwarding readiness, WB result selection
or upstream stalls. The branch already has all those side effects disabled
by decoding. No new source-value comparator or extra register is needed.
Do not propagate the completed branch fault back to EX/MEM controls.
Keep load/store misalignment and jump faults on their existing side-effect
suppression paths. This defers conditional trap reporting, never drops it.

Retain EX's exact misalign_fault expression for architectural pc_next,
which already chooses PC+4 on a taken misaligned branch. Its branch-only
use now feeds verification metadata, not timed eligibility. Taken aligned
branches report their target, untaken branches report PC+4 even when the
unused target is misaligned, and a taken misaligned branch traps with
PC+4. JAL/JALR retain current fault behavior and suppressed links. Capture
the completed branch trap only as the owning MEM instruction advances;
dmem holds retain its record and retirement remains exactly once. RVFI
sources, results, instruction, successor and contiguous order remain exact.

Keep control-only EX squash, reset/hold rules, older registered recovery
priority, divider request/result gating and younger training suppression.
No wrong-path instruction may regain eligibility after the fault-path
change. Add assertions that a decoded conditional branch never has any
register/memory side-effect control, and that its retirement trap matches
the exact captured taken-target fault plus original decoder legality.
Do not assume those properties in formal or weaken existing tests.

The intended timing gain is reducing fanout on forwarded branch operands
and eliminating the branch comparator's dependency into ctrl.reg_write,
ctrl.is_illegal, fwd_ready and divider metadata eligibility registers.
The champion's worst path is WB-to-EX ALU, so reducing nearby control and
forwarding loading may improve that path even though arithmetic is fixed.
Forecast six percent fitness gain with low confidence at unchanged cycles.

fanout reduction does not clear the acceptance margin. Require measured
fitness above 234.39814 iter/sec; at 4416239 cycles median Gowin Fmax must
exceed about 103.52 MHz. Measure all three placement options and canonical
marker-bounded CoreMark, preserving every formal/cosim/CRC/UART/bounds
check, nret=1, external IO, RV32IM arithmetic and forward progress.

the unnecessary conditional-fault fanout rather than enlarging prediction
state or moving the prediction comparison/recovery boundary.

title: Compact dual-read distributed-RAM register file with reset validity
motivation:
The champion scores 237.23 iter/sec at 97.373 MHz and 4,104,522 marked
CoreMark cycles. Its integer register file uses 992 individually reset
flip-flops and wide asynchronous read muxes. Each WB data bit fans out
to every writable word as well as bypass consumers. A physically smaller
register-file topology can reduce that writeback fanout and congestion
without increasing pipeline depth or changing dependency latency.
LESSONS.md is absent. Prior structural experiments were reviewed:
blocking multiplication, an additional operand stage, replicated EX banks
and arithmetic reconstruction all regressed; the two-entry fetch queue
is retained. A multiplier-preparation probe removed the DSP critical
path but reached only 95.937 MHz. Four/eight-entry fetch buffers saved
about 1.5 percent cycles and worsened timing. Neither is proposed.

CoreMark cycles. Its integer register file uses 992 individually reset
flip-flops and wide asynchronous read muxes. Each WB data bit fans out

without increasing pipeline depth or changing dependency latency.
LESSONS.md is absent. Prior structural experiments were reviewed:

and arithmetic reconstruction all regressed; the two-entry fetch queue

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace only the flop-based integer register file with one behavioral
distributed-RAM array exposing two asynchronous read ports and one
synchronous write port. Let Gowin infer mirrored physical read banks
from this shared array, rather than manually declaring duplicated words. This is
one structural change to register storage and operand delivery. Preserve
the existing module ports, ID/EX operand registers, writeback boundary,
forwarding topology, instruction stages and all instruction latencies.

Use Gowin's supported syn_ramstyle="distributed_ram" attribute on the
memory arrays; "distributed" is invalid and silently permits BSRAM
inference, which a private probe found substantially slower. Use portable
behavioral memory RTL with asynchronous reads and synchronous writes so
Verilator and Yosys elaborate the same architectural storage. Do not use
a vendor-only behavioral shortcut or add a simulation/formal bypass.
No synchronous-read BSRAM may absorb the existing ID/EX operand boundary.

Keep the storage arrays free of reset. Instead, maintain one resettable
initialized bit per architectural word, shared across the mirrored
copies. Synchronous reset clears every bit. A nonzero enabled write when
reset is low updates the array and sets only its owning initialized bit. Mask unwritten locations to zero on both read ports. Thus every
register still observably clears on every reset, including repeated resets
and reads of stale RAM contents, while the RAM itself retains inferable
write behavior. x0 always reads zero, ignores writes and never gains an
initialized bit. Reset wins over memory writes and initialized-bit sets.

Preserve same-cycle write-first behavior exactly: an enabled nonzero WB
write matching either read address supplies w_data immediately, even
before the synchronous edge. Both ports may bypass together. Preserve the
current combinational behavior during reset as well as post-edge zeroing;
do not qualify the read bypass with reset if that changes the original
interface. A disabled write never changes RAM or initialized state.

Use exactly one 32-by-32 behavioral storage declaration with two indexed
asynchronous reads. After x0 qualification, give same-cycle WB bypass
priority over initialized-word data, then return zero for an unwritten
word. Keep one shared resettable validity vector and the original
read-output priority expression. Do not use four/eight-entry fetch
buffers, split the read output into masked-OR terms or manually partition
the RAM into smaller address banks: private probes of those variants
failed to improve median timing. Use the shared array to expose the
actual one-write/two-read storage topology to synthesis, with no new
pipeline register, clock phase, operand stall or decode-address hold.
Keep all 32 architectural data bits and stable output behavior for held
decode addresses. Dmem/divider holds retain existing ID/EX and WB
forwarding behavior; the register file still writes only valid WB records.

All ordinary, shift and M-extension arithmetic, ALTOPS formulas, fetch
queue/prediction/recovery, trap and decoder discipline, memory requests,
exact RVFI sources/results/successors, nret=1 ports and contiguous order
remain architectural. Add no new early retirement or memory speculation.
Change no evaluator, wrapper, benchmark source or formal configuration.

A private unsplit distributed-RAM prototype used the unchanged vendor
flow and measured options 0/1/2 at 94.272/100.824/100.824 MHz, median
100.824 MHz. Option 0 used 2917 logic cells, 955 FFs, 32 LUT-RAM cells,
four BSRAMs and two DSPs, versus the champion's 3670 logic cells and
1916 FFs. The reset-validity implementation passed all eight full
retirement cosim runs (selftest/random1/2/3, each zero-wait and both bus
stalls), and canonical CoreMark CRCs/UART/markers/bounds with unchanged
4,104,522 cycles. That unsplit implementation improves fitness only
about 3.5 percent and does not itself clear acceptance. The final shared-array
topology must be measured; no qualifying result is claimed by these

title: Share B/J prediction targets through a four-bit carry-select network
motivation:
The current champion scores 237.23 iter/sec using a small agree predictor
and a two-entry elastic fetch queue. Predictor history shows that tagged
target tables and recovery retiming lose fitness, while instruction-qualified
direct prediction preserves correctness with only one direction bit of
metadata. The remaining direct-prediction fetch path computes a 12-bit
branch sum and a 20-bit JAL sum before choosing upper address corrections
and the successor. Shorten this predictor target-generation path while
retaining its successful policy and recovery schedule. LESSONS.md is absent.

hypothesis.motivation:
The current champion scores 237.23 iter/sec using a small agree predictor
and a two-entry elastic fetch queue. Predictor history shows that tagged
target tables and recovery retiming lose fitness, while instruction-qualified
direct prediction preserves correctness with only one direction bit of
metadata. The remaining direct-prediction fetch path computes a 12-bit
branch sum and a 20-bit JAL sum before choosing upper address corrections
and the successor. Shorten this predictor target-generation path while
retaining its successful policy and recovery schedule. LESSONS.md is absent.
hypothesis.hypothesis:
Keep the current sixteen-counter agree predictor, folded PC index, static
bias, instruction qualification, queue, training boundary and registered
recovery. Replace only B/J prediction target arithmetic in if_stage with
a shared exact block carry-select addition network. Build the selected
sign-extended B/J displacement from raw instruction bits. Compute both
carry-in possibilities for each of eight four-bit blocks in parallel,
derive group propagate/generate independently of the sum selections,
and use a balanced prefix network to determine every block's true carry.
Select each block's already computed sum using that carry. Cover all 32
architectural address bits and modulo-2^32 overflow; never truncate PCs
or assume that CoreMark remains within a page. Retain four-bit blocks;
the private probes of other widths and successor muxes were worse.

Use raw instr[3] to select J-immediate wiring for JAL (0x6f) and
B-immediate wiring for BRANCH (0x63); this distinguishes the two positively
validated direct opcodes without putting full opcode decode before the
adder. Other encodings cannot use its output because legal_branch/legal_jal
still qualify prediction. For block k, compute five-bit z = pc_block +
displacement_block and o = pc_block + displacement_block + 1 in parallel.
Set G[k] = z[4] and P[k] = AND-reduction(pc_block XOR displacement_block).
Use three prefix levels at block distances 1, 2 and 4: G' = G OR (P AND
earlier_G), P' = P AND earlier_P, with low nodes passed through unchanged.
Block zero uses carry-in zero; each later block uses the previous block's
final prefix G. Select z[3:0] or o[3:0] with that carry. Use ordinary
conditional sum selection, XOR-based propagation and the existing five
masked PC terms; the probes of other formulations were not retained.

The computed direct target is authoritative for the instruction-qualified
fetch prediction. B/J immediate wiring may be selected in parallel with
opcode validation, but qualification must still reject reserved branches
and misaligned destinations. JAL remains always taken when legal/aligned;
JALR remains unpredicted. Agreement determines branch direction exactly
as today. Preserve independent PC+4, held PC and registered repair terms
in the existing balanced masked successor selection. No target cache,
wide new pipeline metadata or arithmetic changes outside prediction are
required. Raw instruction data and target sums remain independent of
ready, flush and recovery, with those controls affecting only acceptance.

Preserve queue admission, empty bypass, carried predicted_taken and the
exactly-once MEM-qualified counter update. Accepted older recovery retains
priority over imem unavailability and younger dependencies/divider holds.
EX continues computing architectural successors and detecting alignment
faults using the original captured PC and instruction. No direct prediction
may depend on a remembered instruction or target. Verify the new adder for
arbitrary 32-bit PCs and signed B/J offsets against exact full addition,
including carry boundaries, wraparound and targets with low bit 1 set.

An isolated prototype of this exact four-bit construction measured Gowin
options 0/1/2 at 98.457/101.095/101.095 MHz, median 101.095 MHz. Option 0
used 3645 LUTs and 1916 FFs, versus the champion's 3670 LUTs and 1916 FFs,
with the same four BSRAMs and two DSPs. The unchanged CoreMark validator
accepted all canonical CRCs, UART success, ten iterations, MMIO brackets
and no out-of-bounds access. The marked cycle count remained 4104522.
Independent Yosys SAT proved the block network equivalent to full addition
for arbitrary 32-bit inputs; both existing predictor unit runners passed.
Full pipeline formal and retirement-reference cosim remain implementation
gates and have not been replaced by that arithmetic equivalence proof.

The measured product is 246.30152 iter/sec, a 3.82393 percent gain. Forecast
a rounded four percent gain with low confidence. This private prototype
does NOT yet clear the 4.6 percent acceptance margin; its result is evidence
for an incremental predictor improvement, not a claim of acceptance. The
principal limitation is that MEM multiplication still sets the clock,
while predictor changes alter area and routing of other near-critical
paths. Do not attribute the full clock change solely to the target adder.
At the champion's 4104522 marked cycles, the 4.6 percent margin requires
fitness above 248.14258 iter/sec and median Fmax above about 101.85 MHz.
Require actual three-option vendor timing and canonical marker-bounded
CoreMark, plus unchanged formal/cosim/CRC/UART/bounds checks. Preserve all
RV32IM arithmetic, decoder default-illegal behavior, traps, forward progress,
nret=1 and the complete external memory and RVFI contracts.
